```text
1	# yth — search your YouTube watch history
2	
3	`yth` is a local-first CLI + Television (`tv`) picker for your own YouTube watch history.
4	YouTube's native `/feed/history` search only matches titles; `yth` indexes **titles,
5	channels, descriptions, and caption text** in a local sqlite database and searches them with
6	FTS5 — so "I know I watched something about X" becomes a one-line query. It's the
7	gh-select-style twin pattern used by `mlf` + `tv mlflow` and [`fleet hosts`](fleet-hosts.md).
8	
9	Binary: `dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_yth` (→ `~/.dotfiles/bin/yth`). Modules: `scripts/yth/`.
10	Picker twin: `tv yth` (`dot_config/television/cable/yth.toml`).
11	
12	## Install
13	
14	Deployed automatically by chezmoi:
15	
16	- `yth` self-bootstraps its Python deps via a `uv run --script` shebang (PEP 723 inline
17	  metadata declaring `yt-dlp`, `tyro`, `rich`, `platformdirs`) — no separate install step.
18	- `yt-dlp` is **also** installed as a standalone binary by the `python_uv_tools` ansible
19	  role (same dual pattern as `mlflow` ↔ `mlf`), so `yt-dlp` is on PATH independently.
20	- Needs `uv` on PATH; `bat` for the `tv yth` preview pane; `ffmpeg` (already via the
21	  `media_tools` role) is optional (only for muxing, which `yth` doesn't do).
22	
23	## Two data sources (and why)
24	
25	Your watch history is **not** in the YouTube Data API (removed ~2016). `yth` gets it two ways:
26	
27	| Source | Command | Cookies? | Coverage | Timestamps |
28	|---|---|---|---|---|
29	| **Google Takeout** (primary) | `yth import-takeout <file>` | no | full multi-year history | exact (from the export) |
30	| **yt-dlp `:ythistory`** (secondary) | `yth sync` | **yes** | recent page-loadable window only | approximate (sync time) |
31	
32	Export from [Google Takeout](https://takeout.google.com/) → *YouTube and YouTube Music* →
33	history → **JSON** format → `watch-history.json`. Import is idempotent: re-importing the
34	same (or an overlapping) export adds nothing. Use `sync` for quick incremental top-ups
35	between exports; Takeout stays the source of truth.
36	
37	## Quick start
38	
39	```bash
40	yth import-takeout ~/Downloads/watch-history.json   # backfill (cookie-free)
41	yth enrich --limit 500                              # fill descriptions/durations (public)
42	yth fetch-subs --recent 100                         # index captions for recent videos
43	yth search "rust async"                             # search title/channel/description
44	yth search "borrow checker" --subs                  # also search caption text
45	tv yth                                              # fuzzy-pick the whole history
46	```
47	
48	## Subcommands
49	
50	| Command | What it does |
51	|---|---|
52	| `import-takeout <file>` | Backfill from a Takeout `watch-history.json` (JSON only). Idempotent. |
53	| `sync [--limit N] [--full]` | Incremental `:ythistory` sync (needs cookies). Walks newest→cursor. |
54	| `enrich [--limit N \| --all] [--cookies] [--force]` | Fetch title/description/duration/upload_date. Cookie-free for public videos. Permanent failures (removed/private) are stamped; transient (bot-check/429) retry next run. |
55	| `fetch-subs <id>… \| --recent N \| --all [--cookies] [--langs …]` | Download manual+auto captions, flatten VTT→text, index. |
56	| `search <query> [--subs] [--json] [--limit N] [--raw]` | FTS5 search. `--subs` also matches captions; `--raw` uses native FTS5 syntax. |
57	| `list [--tsv] [--limit N]` | List history newest-first. `--tsv` is the `tv yth` source. |
58	| `show <id> [--json]` | One-video detail (DB-only, no network). Powers the tv preview. |
59	| `open <id>` / `copy <id>` / `play <id>` | Open in browser / copy URL / play (mpv if configured, else browser). |
60	
61	## Cookies (only `sync` + restricted videos)
62	
63	**Public videos need no cookies** — `enrich` and `fetch-subs` of public content work
64	unauthenticated. Cookies are required only for `yth sync` (your account-private history)
65	and for members-only / age-restricted / private videos.
66	
67	yt-dlp's `--cookies-from-browser` knows `brave, chrome, chromium, edge, firefox, opera,
68	safari, vivaldi, whale` — **not** `arc` or `zen` (both are forks). Handle them like this:
69	
70	| Browser | Mechanism | Config |
71	|---|---|---|
72	| **Zen** (Firefox fork) | yt-dlp reads Firefox-format `cookies.sqlite` from an explicit profile path. Auto-detected if Zen is installed. | `from_browser = "firefox:/path/to/zen/Profiles/<profile>"` |
73	| **Arc** (Chromium fork) | The `chrome` keyword derives the Keychain service name *"Chrome Safe Storage"*; Arc's is *"Arc Safe Storage"* and there's no flag to override it, so keyword extraction can't decrypt Arc cookies on macOS. Export a `cookies.txt` instead. | `cookiefile = "~/.config/yth/cookies.txt"` |
74	| Standard Chrome/Firefox/… | Use the keyword directly. | `from_browser = "firefox"` (or `chrome`, …) |
75	
76	To export Arc cookies: install the **"Get cookies.txt LOCALLY"** extension (Arc is Chromium,
77	so Chrome Web Store extensions install), visit `youtube.com` logged in, Export → save as
78	`~/.config/yth/cookies.txt`. These expire; re-export periodically.
79	
80	## The `tv yth` channel
81	
82	`tv yth` (or bare `yth`) opens a fuzzy picker over `yth list --tsv`. Television's source is
83	single-shot and never sees the live query, so the channel fuzzy-filters the **title/channel
84	display string** only — **caption/description search stays in `yth search --subs`**.
85	
86	| Key | Action |
87	|---|---|
88	| `Enter` / `Ctrl+O` / `Alt+B` | Open the video in the browser |
89	| `Ctrl+Y` | Copy the video URL |
90	| `Alt+P` | Play (mpv if configured, else browser) |
91	| `Alt+S` | Fetch captions for this video, then show detail |
92	| `Alt+J` | Dump the video's JSON detail |
93	
94	`Alt+` (not `Ctrl+`) is used for new actions because this repo's tmux prefix is `Ctrl+b` —
95	a `ctrl-b` binding would be swallowed before tv saw it. The `o/b/y/p/s/j` mnemonics are the
96	SSOT for a future `yth tui`.
97	
98	## Config — `~/.config/yth/config.toml`
99	
100	```toml
101	# cookiefile   = "~/.config/yth/cookies.txt"                    # Arc / any browser (export)
102	# from_browser = "firefox:/…/zen/Profiles/xxxx.Default"        # Zen (auto-detected if unset)
103	langs        = ["en", "en-US"]                                 # subtitle languages to fetch
104	open_target  = "browser"                                       # browser | mpv
105	```
106	
107	## Storage
108	
109	Resolved via `platformdirs` (honours `XDG_*`): DB at `~/.local/share/yth/history.db`, config
110	at `~/.config/yth/config.toml`, cache at `~/.cache/yth/`. Set `$YTH_DB` to override the DB
111	path (used by tests). Schema: `videos` (+ `videos_fts`), `watch_events` (one row per watch;
112	stats via the `video_stats` view), `subtitles` (+ `subtitles_fts`), `meta`. FTS is
113	external-content with triggers, so `enrich`/`fetch-subs` UPDATEs re-index automatically.
114	
115	## Cross-file invariants
116	
117	Touching `yth` means keeping these in sync (see the `CLAUDE.md` cross-file table row):
118	
119	1. `dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_yth` — launcher (PEP723 deps + dict-dispatch). Shared helpers
120	   live in `scripts/yth/__init__.py`; leaf subcommands in `scripts/yth/*.py`.
121	2. `dot_config/television/cable/yth.toml` — the `o/b/y/p/s/j` mnemonics mirror any future
122	   `yth tui`; new actions use `Alt+`.
123	3. `dot_config/zsh/tools/53_yth_completion.zsh` + `dot_config/bash/53_yth_completion.bash` —
124	   keep the two in sync (Strategy B).
125	4. `dot_ansible/roles/python_uv_tools/defaults/main.yml` — the `yt-dlp` entry (dual with the
126	   launcher PEP723 block).
127	5. Docs: this page (+ `yth.zh-TW.md`), `docs/shells/aliases.md`, `docs/zsh/zsh-completions.md`
128	   §F, `docs/this_repo/tool-managers.md` A–Z + uv inventory, `mkdocs.yml` nav,
129	   `dot_agents/skills/chezmoi-dotfiles/SKILL.md.tmpl`.
130	
131	## Troubleshooting
132	
133	- **`Sign in to confirm you're not a bot`** on `enrich`/`fetch-subs`/`sync` — YouTube
134	  bot-check, common from datacenter IPs. It's treated as transient (not stamped), so it
135	  retries next run. Configure cookies (`--cookies` for enrich/fetch-subs) or run from a
136	  residential IP.
137	- **`no captions`** — the video genuinely has no subtitles in the configured `langs`. Add
138	  langs (`--langs en,en-orig,zh-Hant`) or accept it (the video is stamped so it won't retry;
139	  `--force` to retry).
140	- **`yth sync: no cookie source configured`** — expected until you set `cookiefile` or
141	  `from_browser`. Prefer `yth import-takeout` for full history (no cookies needed).
142	- **Empty `tv yth`** — no history imported yet. Run `yth import-takeout` or `yth sync`.
143
```

```text
1	"""yth fetch-subs — download + index subtitle text for videos.
2	
3	Fetches manual subs (falling back to auto-captions) via yt-dlp, flattens the
4	VTT to deduplicated plain text (see ``vtt_to_text``), and stores it so
5	``yth search --subs`` can match what was *said* in a video. **Cookie-free by
6	default** for public videos.
7	
8	Selection (one required):
9	  <id>...        explicit video ids
10	  --recent N     the N most-recently-watched pending videos
11	  --all          every pending video
12	
13	"Pending" = ``subs_fetched_at IS NULL``; a video with no available captions is
14	still stamped so it isn't retried (override with ``--force``). Bulk fetching is
15	sequential + throttled to avoid YouTube rate-limiting.
16	"""
17	from __future__ import annotations
18	
19	import glob
20	import os
21	import sys
22	import tempfile
23	import time
24	from dataclasses import dataclass, field
25	from typing import Annotated
26	
27	import tyro
28	
29	from scripts.yth import connect, cookie_opts, load_config, now_iso, video_url, vtt_to_text, ytdl
30	
31	
32	@dataclass
33	class Args:
34	    video_ids: Annotated[
35	        list[str],
36	        tyro.conf.Positional,
37	        tyro.conf.arg(help="Explicit video ids (omit to use --recent/--all)."),
38	    ] = field(default_factory=list)
39	    recent: Annotated[
40	        int, tyro.conf.arg(help="Fetch the N most-recently-watched pending videos.")
41	    ] = 0
42	    all: Annotated[bool, tyro.conf.arg(help="Fetch every pending video.")] = False
43	    force: Annotated[
44	        bool, tyro.conf.arg(help="Refetch even if subs were already fetched.")
45	    ] = False
46	    cookies: Annotated[
47	        bool, tyro.conf.arg(help="Use the configured cookie source (restricted videos).")
48	    ] = False
49	    langs: Annotated[
50	        list[str],
51	        tyro.conf.arg(help="Subtitle langs (default: from config, else en/en-US)."),
52	    ] = field(default_factory=list)
53	    sleep: Annotated[
54	        float, tyro.conf.arg(help="Seconds to pause between videos (rate-limit).")
55	    ] = 1.5
56	
57	
58	def _select(con, args: Args) -> list[str]:
59	    if args.video_ids:
60	        return [v.strip() for v in args.video_ids if v.strip()]
61	    where = "" if args.force else "WHERE v.subs_fetched_at IS NULL"
62	    if args.all:
63	        rows = con.execute(
64	            f"SELECT v.video_id FROM videos v "
65	            f"LEFT JOIN video_stats s ON s.video_id=v.video_id {where} "
66	            f"ORDER BY (s.last_watched IS NULL), s.last_watched DESC"
67	        ).fetchall()
68	        return [r["video_id"] for r in rows]
69	    if args.recent > 0:
70	        rows = con.execute(
71	            f"SELECT v.video_id FROM videos v "
72	            f"LEFT JOIN video_stats s ON s.video_id=v.video_id {where} "
73	            f"ORDER BY (s.last_watched IS NULL), s.last_watched DESC LIMIT ?",
74	            (args.recent,),
75	        ).fetchall()
76	        return [r["video_id"] for r in rows]
77	    return []
78	
79	
80	def fetch_subs_for(yt_dlp, vid: str, langs: list[str], cookies: dict) -> dict[str, str]:
81	    """Return {lang: plaintext} for one video. Empty dict if no captions."""
82	    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as td:
83	        opts = {
84	            "skip_download": True,
85	            "writesubtitles": True,
86	            "writeautomaticsub": True,
87	            "subtitleslangs": langs,
88	            "subtitlesformat": "vtt",
89	            "outtmpl": os.path.join(td, "%(id)s.%(ext)s"),
90	            "quiet": True,
91	            "no_warnings": True,
92	            "sleep_interval_subtitles": 1,
93	            **cookies,
94	        }
95	        with yt_dlp.YoutubeDL(opts) as ydl:
96	            ydl.download([video_url(vid)])
97	        out: dict[str, str] = {}
98	        for path in sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(td, "*.vtt"))):
99	            parts = os.path.basename(path).split(".")
100	            lang = parts[-2] if len(parts) >= 3 else "und"
101	            text = vtt_to_text(open(path, encoding="utf-8").read())
102	            if text:
103	                out[lang] = text
104	        return out
105	
106	
107	def cli(args: Args) -> int:
108	    con = connect()
109	    targets = _select(con, args)
110	    if not targets:
111	        print(
112	            "yth fetch-subs: no target videos. Pass ids, or --recent N / --all.",
113	            file=sys.stderr,
114	        )
115	        return 2
116	
117	    cfg = load_config()
118	    langs = args.langs or cfg.get("langs") or ["en", "en-US"]
119	    cookies = cookie_opts(cfg) if args.cookies else {}
120	    yt_dlp = ytdl()
121	
122	    with_subs = no_subs = failed = 0
123	    total = len(targets)
124	    for i, vid in enumerate(targets, 1):
125	        try:
126	            subs = fetch_subs_for(yt_dlp, vid, langs, cookies)
127	        except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001
128	            failed += 1
129	            msg = str(e).splitlines()[0][:120] if str(e) else type(e).__name__
130	            print(f"  [{i}/{total}] {vid} ✗ {msg}", file=sys.stderr)
131	        else:
132	            for lang, text in subs.items():
133	                con.execute(
134	                    "INSERT INTO subtitles(video_id, lang, text, fetched_at) "
135	                    "VALUES(?, ?, ?, ?) "
136	                    "ON CONFLICT(video_id, lang) DO UPDATE SET "
137	                    "  text=excluded.text, fetched_at=excluded.fetched_at",
138	                    (vid, lang, text, now_iso()),
139	                )
140	            con.execute(
141	                "UPDATE videos SET subs_fetched_at=? WHERE video_id=?", (now_iso(), vid)
142	            )
143	            con.commit()
144	            if subs:
145	                with_subs += 1
146	                langs_got = ", ".join(subs)
147	                print(f"  [{i}/{total}] {vid} ✓ {langs_got}", file=sys.stderr)
148	            else:
149	                no_subs += 1
150	                print(f"  [{i}/{total}] {vid} — no captions", file=sys.stderr)
151	        if args.sleep and i < total:
152	            time.sleep(args.sleep)
153	
154	    print(
155	        f"yth fetch-subs: {with_subs} with captions, {no_subs} without, {failed} failed.",
156	        file=sys.stderr,
157	    )
158	    return 0
159	
160	
161	def main() -> int:
162	    return cli(tyro.cli(Args, prog="yth fetch-subs"))
163	
164	
165	if __name__ == "__main__":
166	    sys.exit(main())
167
```
</details></tool-use>

## 結論：目前**沒有**下載影音的功能，只有「抓字幕進資料庫」

分成三層來看：

**1. `yth` CLI（`dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_yth` + `scripts/yth/`）**
它是 **YouTube 觀看紀錄搜尋工具**，不是下載器。唯一碰媒體的是 `yth fetch-subs`，而且：

- `scripts/yth/fetch_subs.py:83` 明確設 `"skip_download": True` — 從不下載影音
- 字幕抓成 VTT 後在 `TemporaryDirectory` 裡就地 flatten 成純文字，寫進 sqlite 的 `subtitles` 表供 FTS5 搜尋，**檔案隨 temp dir 一起刪掉**，不會留下 `.srt`/`.vtt` 給你
- 文件也寫死了這個界線：`docs/tools/yth.md:21` — 「`ffmpeg` … is optional (only for muxing, which `yth` doesn't do)」

**2. Shell alias / 函式**
`dot_config/{shell,zsh,bash}/` 裡完全沒有 `ytmp3` 之類的 wrapper，grep 只命中兩個 `yth` completion 檔。也沒有 `dot_config/yt-dlp/config` 這種 SSOT 設定檔。

**3. `yt-dlp` 本體**
有裝、在 PATH 上（`~/.local/bin/yt-dlp`，2026.07.04，由 `python_uv_tools` role 裝），`ffmpeg` 也有（`/usr/local/bin/ffmpeg`）。所以能力在，只是沒有包裝。

## 現在就能用的裸命令

同時留 mp4 + 產 mp3（`-k` 讓 audio 抽取後保留原始 video）：

```bash
yt-dlp -f "bv*+ba/b" --merge-output-format mp4 \
       -x --audio-format mp3 --keep-video \
       --write-subs --write-auto-subs --sub-langs "en,zh-Hant" --convert-subs srt \
       -o "%(title)s.%(ext)s" "<URL>"
```

只要字幕不要影片：加 `--skip-download`。想把字幕燒進 mp4 容器：`--embed-subs`（拿掉 `--write-subs` 就不落地成獨立檔）。

## 要不要補上？

如果你想要這個變成 repo 的一級功能，兩條路線差很多，我建議先確認你要哪個：

- **輕量**：`dot_config/yt-dlp/config` 放預設參數（格式、輸出模板、字幕語言）+ 一兩個 shell 函式（`ytmp3` / `ytmp4`），成本小、不用動 `yth`。
- **整合進 `yth`**：加 `yth get <id> --audio/--video/--subs`，讓下載跟觀看紀錄 DB 連動（例如記錄已下載路徑）。這會踩到 CLAUDE.md 那條 `yth` 跨檔不變量 —— launcher、`cable/yth.toml` 的 `Alt+` 鍵、兩個 shell completion、docs（含 `.zh-TW`）都要同步改。

要哪一個跟我說，我直接做。

114	    """Rewrite argv and hand off to a leaf module's tyro-based main()."""
115	    sys.argv = [prog, *args]

166	    leaves = {

168	        "sync": ("sync", "yth sync"),

"""appsrc — detect how an installed app / CLI was installed & managed.

There is no single OS command that tells you whether an app came from a
Homebrew cask, the Mac App Store, a direct-download dmg/pkg, apt, snap,
flatpak, an AppImage, or a language package manager. This tool combines
several signals, ordered by specificity, and captures the evidence.

Subcommands (positional, default `scan`):
  scan            Batch-inventory installed GUI apps + CLI tools, attribute

  which <name>    which-style single lookup, always live (no cache). NAME may
                  be a shell command (docker) OR a GUI app name ("Google
                  Chrome") — auto-detected. Prints source + evidence.

scan flags:
  --json                     Emit JSON (list of records) instead of a table.
  --kind {gui,cli,all}       Restrict inventory (default: all).
  --source FILTER            Only rows whose source id/label matches FILTER.
  -r, --refresh              Recompute everything, ignore cache.
  --no-cache                 Don't read or write the cache.
  --list-names               Print GUI app names only (used by completions).

which flags:
  --json                     Emit the single record as JSON.
  --path PATH                Classify PATH directly (skip name resolution).

  `_MASReceipt` is NOT a reliable App Store discriminator (it exists in some

88	def fmt_duration(secs: int | None) -> str:
89	    """Seconds → ``H:MM:SS`` / ``M:SS`` (or ``-``)."""
90	    if not secs:
91	        return "-"
92	    secs = int(secs)
93	    h, rem = divmod(secs, 3600)

101	    Takeout ``time`` fields look like ``2024-01-02T03:04:05.678Z``. We accept
102	    the trailing ``Z`` (Python <3.11 datetime.fromisoformat can't) and drop
103	    sub-second precision so ``watch_events`` de-dupes cleanly.

223	            )
224	            raise SystemExit(3) from e
225	        raise
226	    con.commit()
227	    return con

230	def meta_get(con, key: str, default: str | None = None) -> str | None:
231	    row = con.execute("SELECT value FROM meta WHERE key=?", (key,)).fetchone()
232	    return row["value"] if row else default
233	
234	
235	def meta_set(con, key: str, value: str) -> None:
236	    con.execute(
237	        "INSERT INTO meta(key, value) VALUES(?, ?) "
238	        "ON CONFLICT(key) DO UPDATE SET value=excluded.value",
239	        (key, value),
240	    )

243	# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
244	# URLs / ids
245	# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
246	def extract_video_id(url: str | None) -> str | None:
247	    """Pull an 11-char YouTube id out of a watch/short/embed/youtu.be URL.
248	
249	    Returns None for non-video rows (Google search entries, removed-video
250	    placeholders, anything without a recognisable id) so callers can skip
251	    them. Also accepts a bare id.
252	    """
253	    if not url:
254	        return None
255	    url = url.strip()
256	    if VIDEO_ID_RE.match(url):
257	        return url
258	
259	    from urllib.parse import parse_qs, urlparse
260	
261	    try:
262	        u = urlparse(url)
263	    except ValueError:
264	        return None
265	    host = (u.hostname or "").lower().removeprefix("www.")
266	
267	    if host == "youtu.be":
268	        cand = u.path.lstrip("/").split("/")[0]
269	        return cand if VIDEO_ID_RE.match(cand) else None
270	
271	    if host in ("youtube.com", "m.youtube.com", "music.youtube.com"):
272	        if u.path == "/watch":
273	            vals = parse_qs(u.query).get("v", [])
274	            cand = vals[0] if vals else ""
275	            return cand if VIDEO_ID_RE.match(cand) else None
276	        for prefix in ("/shorts/", "/embed/", "/live/", "/v/"):
277	            if u.path.startswith(prefix):
278	                cand = u.path[len(prefix):].split("/")[0]
279	                return cand if VIDEO_ID_RE.match(cand) else None
280	    return None
281	
282	
283	def video_url(video_id: str) -> str:
284	    """Canonical watch URL (works for shorts too; opens in the app/site)."""
285	    return f"https://www.youtube.com/watch?v={video_id}"
286	
287	
288	# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
289	# Config + cookies
290	# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
291	def load_config() -> dict:
292	    """Read config.toml (if present); fill defaults; auto-detect Zen cookies.
293	
294	    Keys: ``cookiefile`` (Arc → exported cookies.txt) XOR ``from_browser``
295	    (e.g. ``firefox:/path/to/zen/profile``); ``langs`` (subtitle langs);
296	    ``open_target`` (``browser`` | ``mpv``).
297	    """
298	    cfg: dict = {}
299	    path = config_dir() / "config.toml"
300	    if path.is_file():
301	        import tomllib
302	
303	        try:
304	            cfg = tomllib.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
305	        except tomllib.TOMLDecodeError as e:
306	            print(f"yth: ignoring malformed {path}: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
307	            cfg = {}
308	
309	    if not cfg.get("cookiefile") and not cfg.get("from_browser"):
310	        zen = _detect_zen_profile()
311	        if zen:
312	            cfg["from_browser"] = f"firefox:{zen}"
313	
314	    cfg.setdefault("langs", ["en", "en-US"])
315	    cfg.setdefault("open_target", "browser")
316	    return cfg
317	
318	
319	def _detect_zen_profile() -> str | None:
320	    """Best-effort path to a Zen (Firefox fork) profile dir with cookies.
321	
322	    macOS: ``~/Library/Application Support/zen/Profiles/*/cookies.sqlite``.
323	    Linux: ``~/.zen/*/cookies.sqlite``. Returns the profile dir (not the
324	    sqlite file) since that's what yt-dlp's ``firefox:<path>`` wants. None
325	    when Zen isn't installed (the common case on this host).
326	    """
327	    roots = [
328	        Path.home() / "Library" / "Application Support" / "zen" / "Profiles",
329	        Path.home() / ".zen",
330	    ]
331	    for root in roots:
332	        if not root.is_dir():
333	            continue
334	        hits = sorted(root.glob("*/cookies.sqlite"))
335	        if hits:
336	            return str(hits[0].parent)
337	    return None
338	
339	
340	def cookie_opts(cfg: dict) -> dict:
341	    """Translate config into yt-dlp cookie options.
342	
343	    Returns ``{}`` when no cookie source is configured — correct for public
344	    videos (enrich / fetch-subs), which need no auth. ``sync`` and restricted
345	    videos require one of the two keys to be set.
346	    """
347	    if cfg.get("cookiefile"):
348	        return {"cookiefile": os.path.expanduser(cfg["cookiefile"])}
349	    if cfg.get("from_browser"):
350	        browser, _, profile = str(cfg["from_browser"]).partition(":")
351	        return {"cookiesfrombrowser": (browser, profile or None, None, None)}
352	    return {}

355	# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
356	# yt-dlp (lazy)
357	# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
358	def ytdl():
359	    """Lazily import and return the ``yt_dlp`` module.
360	
361	    Kept behind a function so DB-only subcommands never import it (it's the
362	    heaviest dependency and the tv preview path must stay instant).
363	    """
364	    import yt_dlp
365	
366	    return yt_dlp
367	
368	
369	# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
370	# Subtitles
371	# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
372	_VTT_TAG = re.compile(r"<[^>]+>")  # <00:00:01.234>, <c>…</c>, alignment tags
373	
374	
375	def vtt_to_text(vtt: str) -> str:
376	    """Flatten a WebVTT subtitle blob to deduplicated plain text.
377	
378	    Strips the WEBVTT header, cue-timing lines, cue numbers, NOTE/STYLE
379	    blocks and inline ``<…>`` tags, then collapses the rolling-caption
380	    duplication typical of YouTube auto-subs (each cue repeats the previous
381	    visible line) with a simple ``line != last`` guard.
382	    """
383	    out: list[str] = []
384	    last: str | None = None
385	    for raw in vtt.splitlines():
386	        line = raw.strip()
387	        if (
388	            not line
389	            or line == "WEBVTT"
390	            or "-->" in line
391	            or line.isdigit()
392	            or line.startswith(("Kind:", "Language:", "NOTE", "STYLE"))
393	        ):
394	            continue
395	        line = _VTT_TAG.sub("", line).strip()
396	        if line and line != last:
397	            out.append(line)
398	            last = line
399	    return " ".join(out)
400	
401	
402	# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
403	# FTS query building
404	# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
405	def fts_query(text: str) -> str:
406	    """Build a safe FTS5 MATCH string: AND of double-quoted terms.
407	
408	    Raw user input can contain ``-``, ``:``, ``"``, ``*``, ``(`` which are
409	    FTS5 operators and raise ``fts5: syntax error``. Quoting each whitespace
410	    term (doubling embedded quotes) turns everything into literal phrase
411	    tokens. Empty input yields ``""`` which the caller must special-case.
412	    """
413	    terms = [t for t in text.split() if t]
414	    return " ".join('"' + t.replace('"', '""') + '"' for t in terms)
415	
416	
417	# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
418	# Actions: open / copy / play  (used by launcher shims + tv channel parity)
419	# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
420	def open_id(video_id: str) -> int:
421	    """Open the video's watch page in the default browser. Returns exit code."""
422	    ident = video_id.strip()
423	    if not VIDEO_ID_RE.match(ident):
424	        print(f"yth open: not a valid video id: {ident!r}", file=sys.stderr)
425	        return 2
426	    import webbrowser
427	
428	    url = video_url(ident)
429	    print(f"[yth] open: {url}", file=sys.stderr)
430	    if not webbrowser.open(url):
431	        print(
432	            "yth open: no usable browser opener (open/xdg-open/wslview missing).\n"
433	            f"  URL: {url}",
434	            file=sys.stderr,
435	        )
436	        return 1
437	    return 0
438

440	def copy_id(video_id: str) -> int:
441	    """Copy the video URL to the clipboard. Returns exit code.
442	
443	    Provider chain pbcopy → wl-copy → xclip → OSC 52, matching
444	    ``scripts/mlf.copy_id`` and the ``yth.toml [actions.copy-url]`` snippet.
445	    """
446	    ident = video_id.strip()
447	    payload = video_url(ident) if VIDEO_ID_RE.match(ident) else ident
448	    providers = [["pbcopy"], ["wl-copy"], ["xclip", "-selection", "clipboard"]]
449	    for cmd in providers:
450	        if shutil.which(cmd[0]):
451	            try:
452	                subprocess.run(cmd, input=payload, text=True, check=True)
453	            except subprocess.CalledProcessError as e:
454	                print(f"yth copy: {cmd[0]} failed ({e.returncode})", file=sys.stderr)
455	                continue
456	            print(f"[yth] copied via {cmd[0]}: {payload}", file=sys.stderr)
457	            return 0
458	    try:
459	        import base64
460	
461	        b64 = base64.b64encode(payload.encode()).decode()
462	        with open("/dev/tty", "w") as tty:
463	            tty.write(f"\033]52;c;{b64}\007")
464	        print(f"[yth] copied via OSC52: {payload}", file=sys.stderr)
465	        return 0
466	    except OSError as e:
467	        print(f"yth copy: no clipboard provider and OSC52 failed ({e}).", file=sys.stderr)
468	        return 1
469	
470	
471	def play_id(video_id: str, cfg: dict | None = None) -> int:
472	    """Play in mpv when configured + installed, else open in browser."""
473	    ident = video_id.strip()
474	    if not VIDEO_ID_RE.match(ident):
475	        print(f"yth play: not a valid video id: {ident!r}", file=sys.stderr)
476	        return 2
477	    cfg = cfg if cfg is not None else load_config()
478	    url = video_url(ident)
479	    if cfg.get("open_target") == "mpv" and shutil.which("mpv"):
480	        print(f"[yth] mpv: {url}", file=sys.stderr)
481	        return subprocess.run(["mpv", url]).returncode
482	    return open_id(ident)

109-  # the yazi Office previewer. The BARE `markitdown` package ships NO format
110-  # converters — the docx/xlsx/pptx readers live in optional extras, so we pull
111-  # [docx,xlsx,pptx] explicitly (without them it raises MissingDependencyException
112-  # on every Office file). Not [all]: that adds pdf/audio/youtube/azure bloat we
113-  # don't need. Pure Python, single entry point. See docs/tools/office-viewers.md.
114-  - name: markitdown[docx,xlsx,pptx]
115-    binary: markitdown
116-    needs_modern_gcc: true  # [xlsx] pulls pandas 3.x → numpy 2.x (source build needs gcc >= 9 on CentOS 7)

yth.toml
---YTH---
# YouTube watch-history channel for television (tv).
#
# Fast fuzzy picker over your own watch history (`yth list --tsv` is the
# source; tv fuzzy-filters the title/channel display string client-side).
# Deep caption search is NOT here — television's source is single-shot and
# never sees the live query, so it can only match the metadata display line.
# Use `yth search --subs <query>` for caption/description search.
#
# Usage:
#   tv yth
#   yth            # bare `yth` execs `tv yth`
#
# Prerequisites:
#   - `yth` on PATH (dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_yth; needs `uv`).
#   - History populated:  yth import-takeout <watch-history.json>  (and/or
#     `yth sync`, `yth enrich`, `yth fetch-subs`).
#   - `bat` for the preview pane.
#
# TSV columns emitted by `yth list --tsv` (col 0 is the id tv hands to
# preview + actions):
#   0 video_id   1 marker(▶/×N)   2 channel   3 title   4 last_watched   5 dur
#
# Keybindings mirror the b/y/p/s/j single-letter mnemonics a future `yth tui`
# would use (CLAUDE.md cross-file rule). Alt+ is used for new actions because
# this repo's tmux prefix is Ctrl+b — a `ctrl-b` binding would never reach tv.

[metadata]
name = "yth"
description = "YouTube watch history: fuzzy-pick by title/channel, preview metadata + captions"
requirements = ["yth"]

[source]
command = "yth list --tsv"
# Show title + channel (both fuzzy-matchable) with date/duration/marker context.
display = "{split:\\t:3}  ·  {split:\\t:2}  ({split:\\t:4}, {split:\\t:5}) {split:\\t:1}"
output = "{split:\\t:0}"
no_sort = true  # `yth list` already orders by last_watched DESC

[preview]
# DB-only (`yth show` never touches the network) so the pane stays instant.
command = "yth show '{split:\\t:0}' | bat --color=always --plain --paging=never --language=markdown"
header = "{split:\\t:2}  ·  {split:\\t:4}"

[ui]
input_header = "YouTube history"

[ui.preview_panel]
size = 55

[keybindings]
enter = "actions:open"
# Override tv's default ctrl-y (copies the whole display row) with URL-only copy.
ctrl-y = "actions:copy-url"
ctrl-o = "actions:open-browser"
# Alt+B is the "b for browser" mnemonic — Ctrl+B is the tmux prefix, so it
# would be swallowed before tv ever saw it.
alt-b = "actions:open-browser"
alt-p = "actions:play"
alt-s = "actions:subs"
alt-j = "actions:json"

[actions.open]
description = "Open the selected video in the browser"
command = "yth open '{split:\\t:0}'"
mode = "fork"

[actions.open-browser]
description = "Open in browser (mnemonic alias of Enter)"
command = "yth open '{split:\\t:0}'"
mode = "fork"

[actions.copy-url]
description = "Copy the video URL to the clipboard"
command = "yth copy '{split:\\t:0}'"
mode = "fork"

[actions.play]
description = "Play in mpv if configured+installed, else browser"
command = "yth play '{split:\\t:0}'"
mode = "fork"

[actions.subs]
description = "Fetch captions for this video, then show detail"
command = "yth fetch-subs '{split:\\t:0}'; echo; yth show '{split:\\t:0}' | bat --color=always --plain --paging=never --language=markdown | less -R; echo; echo '[Press Enter to exit]'; read -r _"
mode = "execute"

[actions.json]
description = "Dump the video's detail as JSON, paged"
command = "yth show '{split:\\t:0}' --json | bat --color=always --plain --paging=never --language=json | less -R; echo; echo '[Press Enter to exit]'; read -r _"
mode = "execute"
```

```text
1	"""yth search — FTS5 search over watch history.
2	
3	Default matches title / channel / description (ranked title≫channel≫desc via
4	bm25). ``--subs`` additionally matches indexed caption text and shows a
5	snippet. ``--json`` emits structured results for piping. DB-only.
6	
7	The tv channel (`tv yth`) only fuzzy-filters the metadata *display string* —
8	television's source is single-shot and never sees the live query — so deep
9	caption search lives here, in the CLI.
10	"""
11	from __future__ import annotations
12	
13	import json
14	import sys
15	from dataclasses import dataclass, field
16	from typing import Annotated
17	
18	import tyro
19	from rich.console import Console
20	from rich.table import Table
21	
22	from scripts.yth import connect, fts_query, short_date
23	
24	
25	@dataclass
26	class Args:
27	    query: Annotated[
28	        list[str],
29	        tyro.conf.Positional,
30	        tyro.conf.arg(help="Search terms (ANDed). Quote to include spaces."),
31	    ] = field(default_factory=list)
32	    subs: Annotated[
33	        bool, tyro.conf.arg(help="Also search indexed caption text.")
34	    ] = False
35	    json_out: Annotated[
36	        bool, tyro.conf.arg(name="json", help="Emit JSON instead of a table.")
37	    ] = False
38	    limit: Annotated[int, tyro.conf.arg(help="Max results.")] = 50
39	    raw: Annotated[
40	        bool,
41	        tyro.conf.arg(help="Pass the query straight to FTS5 (native MATCH syntax)."),
42	    ] = False
43	
44	
45	def _meta_hits(con, match: str, limit: int):
46	    return con.execute(
47	        """
48	        SELECT v.video_id, v.title, v.channel, s.watch_count, s.last_watched
49	        FROM videos_fts f
50	        JOIN videos v ON v.id = f.rowid
51	        LEFT JOIN video_stats s ON s.video_id = v.video_id
52	        WHERE videos_fts MATCH ?
53	        ORDER BY bm25(videos_fts, 8.0, 4.0, 1.0)
54	        LIMIT ?
55	        """,
56	        (match, limit),
57	    ).fetchall()
58	
59	
60	def _subs_hits(con, match: str, limit: int):
61	    return con.execute(
62	        """
63	        SELECT sub.video_id, v.title, v.channel, s.watch_count, s.last_watched,
64	               snippet(subtitles_fts, 0, '»', '«', '…', 10) AS snip
65	        FROM subtitles_fts sf
66	        JOIN subtitles sub ON sub.id = sf.rowid
67	        JOIN videos v ON v.video_id = sub.video_id
68	        LEFT JOIN video_stats s ON s.video_id = v.video_id
69	        WHERE subtitles_fts MATCH ?
70	        ORDER BY bm25(subtitles_fts)
71	        LIMIT ?
72	        """,
73	        (match, limit),
74	    ).fetchall()
75	
76	
77	def cli(args: Args) -> int:
78	    text = " ".join(args.query).strip()
79	    if not text:
80	        print("yth search: empty query. Try: yth search <terms>", file=sys.stderr)
81	        return 2
82	
83	    match = text if args.raw else fts_query(text)
84	    if not match:
85	        print("yth search: query has no searchable terms.", file=sys.stderr)
86	        return 2
87	
88	    con = connect()
89	    import sqlite3
90	
91	    try:
92	        meta = _meta_hits(con, match, args.limit)
93	        subs = _subs_hits(con, match, args.limit) if args.subs else []
94	    except sqlite3.OperationalError as e:
95	        print(
96	            f"yth search: FTS5 rejected the query ({e}).\n"
97	            "  Drop --raw, or quote special characters.",
98	            file=sys.stderr,
99	        )
100	        return 2
101	
102	    # Merge: metadata hits keep their rank; caption-only hits append. A video
103	    # matched by both is tagged with both sources.
104	    order: list[str] = []
105	    by_id: dict[str, dict] = {}
106	    for r in meta:
107	        by_id[r["video_id"]] = {
108	            "video_id": r["video_id"],
109	            "title": r["title"] or r["video_id"],
110	            "channel": r["channel"] or "-",
111	            "watch_count": r["watch_count"] or 0,
112	            "last_watched": r["last_watched"],
113	            "matched": ["meta"],
114	            "snippet": None,
115	        }
116	        order.append(r["video_id"])
117	    for r in subs:
118	        vid = r["video_id"]
119	        if vid in by_id:
120	            by_id[vid]["matched"].append("subs")
121	            by_id[vid]["snippet"] = r["snip"]
122	        else:
123	            by_id[vid] = {
124	                "video_id": vid,
125	                "title": r["title"] or vid,
126	                "channel": r["channel"] or "-",
127	                "watch_count": r["watch_count"] or 0,

---
# Python CLI tools installed via uv tool install
# Each tool has:
#   - name: package name (can include extras like [cli])
#   - binary: executable name to check for idempotency
#   - with: (optional) additional dependency to install with --with
#   - with_executables_from: (optional) list of packages to install AND
#     expose their entry points in ~/.local/bin (e.g. jupyter-core to get
#     the `jupyter` meta-CLI; `notebook` to get `jupyter-notebook`)
#     NOTE: requires uv >= 0.8.5 (--with-executables-from added in that release)
#     For the meta-CLI dispatch model + the 8 jupyter binaries this exposes,
#     see docs/tools/notebooks.md "The `jupyter` meta-CLI vs standalone binaries".
#     For the auto-upgrade dispatch when uv is too old, see docs/this_repo/uv-bootstrap.md.
#   - extra_binaries: (optional) list of additional binary names that must
#     also exist in ~/.local/bin for the install to be considered complete.
#     Use this whenever `with_executables_from` is set, so adding a new
#     entry-point package later triggers a `--force` reinstall on machines
#     that already have `binary` present from a prior apply. Without this,
#     ansible's `creates:` guard short-circuits the install command and the
#     new exec shims are never written. See
#     pitfalls/uv-tool-install-creates-guard-misses-executables-from.md.
#   - python: (optional) pin Python version (e.g. "3.11" for thefuck)
#   - needs_modern_gcc: (optional, default false) tool transitively pulls
#     numpy 2.x / pandas 3.x / pyarrow which require GCC ≥ 9.3 to compile
#     from source. Skipped on systems where GCC < 9 (e.g. CentOS 7's
#     gcc 4.8.5). uv falls back to source build because numpy 2.x
#     dropped manylinux_2_17 wheels — see
#     pitfalls/centos7-numpy-pandas-source-build.md.

python_uv_tools:
  - name: thefuck
    binary: thefuck
    python: "3.11"  # Python 3.13 removed distutils which thefuck still uses
  - name: apprise
    binary: apprise
  - name: sqlit-tui[ssh]
    binary: sqlit
    needs_modern_gcc: true  # textual-fastdatatable -> pandas -> numpy 2.x
    with:
      - psycopg2-binary
      - pymysql
      - mssql-python
      - pyodbc
      - duckdb
  - name: python-dotenv[cli]
    binary: dotenv
  - name: git-filter-repo
    binary: git-filter-repo
  - name: mlflow
    binary: mlflow
    needs_modern_gcc: true  # sqlalchemy -> greenlet C++ ext needs proper C++11 (CentOS 7 gcc 4.8.5 lacks it by default)
  - name: tmuxp
    binary: tmuxp
  - name: visidata
    binary: vd
    needs_modern_gcc: true  # explicit pandas + pyarrow deps
    with:
      - pandas
      - pyarrow  # Required for parquet/feather/arrow loaders. Note: .feather
                 # files whose schema metadata marks columns as pandas
                 # StringDtype still crash the default PandasSheet path even
                 # with pyarrow installed; the dot_visidatarc override
                 # routes .feather → ArrowSheet to dodge that. See
                 # pitfalls/visidata-feather-stringdtype-numpy-dtype.md.
  - name: copyparty
    binary: copyparty
  - name: trafilatura
    binary: trafilatura
  - name: marimo[recommended,mcp]
    binary: marimo
    needs_modern_gcc: true  # marimo[recommended] -> polars[pyarrow] -> pyarrow -> numpy 2.x
    with:
      - httpx[socks]
  - name: jupyterlab
    binary: jupyter-lab
    needs_modern_gcc: true  # ipykernel -> pyzmq -> Cython-generated C99 (gcc 4.8.5 defaults to gnu89); also marimo[sandbox]/[recommended] chains can pull pyarrow
    with:
      - marimo[sandbox]
      - marimo-jupyter-extension
      - ipykernel
      - ipywidgets
    with_executables_from:
      - notebook       # exposes jupyter-notebook (classic UI, Notebook 7)
      - jupyter-core   # exposes the `jupyter` meta-CLI dispatcher
    extra_binaries:
      - jupyter           # from jupyter-core
      - jupyter-notebook  # from notebook
  # Xonsh: Python-superset shell. Installed as an experimental tertiary shell —
  # never set as login shell (primaryShell schema stays zsh|bash). The bundled
  # xontribs ship inside xonsh's tool venv so `xontrib load <name>` finds them
  # without extra pip work. See docs/shells/xonsh.md.
  - name: xonsh
    binary: xonsh
    with:
      - xontrib-jedi          # Jedi-powered Python tab completion inside xonsh
```

```text
def main() -> int:
    args = parse_args()
    snapshots = _load_snapshots(args.stdin_json, args.raw_stdin, args.host, args.group)

    if args.mode == "json":
        print(json.dumps([asdict(s) for s in snapshots], indent=2, default=str))
        return 0

    if args.mode == "text":
        for snap in snapshots:
            if len(snapshots) > 1:
                err.print(f"[bold]── {snap.host} ──[/bold]")
            if snap.error:
                err.print(f"[red]{snap.host}: {snap.error}[/red]")
                continue
            render_text(snap, use_color=sys.stdout.isatty())
        return 0

    # --- ai mode ---
    prompt = build_prompt(snapshots, multi_host=args.multi_host or len(snapshots) > 1)
    if args.dry_run:
        print(prompt)
        return 0

    prompt_hash = hashlib.sha256(prompt.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()[:16]
    parsed: dict | None = None
    if not args.refresh and not args.no_cache:
        cached, reason = _cache_lookup(prompt_hash)
        if cached is not None and reason == "hit":
            parsed = cached

    if parsed is None:
        agent = detect_agent()
        if agent is None:
            tried = ", ".join(AICAP_AGENT_PRIORITY)
            err.print(f"[red]No coding-agent CLI on PATH (tried: {tried}).[/red]")
            err.print("[dim]Install one, or set AICAP_AGENT=http with AICAP_HTTP_API_KEY.[/dim]")
            return 2
        with err.status(f"[dim]{agent} ({model_for(agent)}) thinking…[/dim]", spinner="dots"):
            reply = invoke_agent(agent, prompt, PQSUM_TIMEOUT)
        parsed = parse_reply(reply)
        if parsed is None:
            err.print("[yellow]pqsum: LLM returned no parseable JSON[/yellow]")
            if reply.strip():
                err.print(f"[dim]{reply.strip()[:400]}[/dim]")
            return 1
        if not args.no_cache:
            _cache_save(prompt_hash, parsed)

    if args.report or args.out or args.clean:
        report = render_report(parsed, snapshots)
        if args.out:
            try:
                Path(args.out).write_text(report, encoding="utf-8")
                err.print(f"[dim]pqsum: wrote {args.out}[/dim]")
            except OSError as e:
                err.print(f"[red]pqsum: failed to write {args.out}: {e}[/red]")
                return 1
        else:
            print(report)
        if args.clean:
            return execute_cleanup(parsed, yes=args.yes)
        return 0

    render_ai(parsed, use_color=sys.stdout.isatty())
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())
```

---
# Media / AV CLI tools role
# Tools: ffmpeg, ImageMagick, exiftool, libvips
# ffmpeg is also vhs's runtime dependency — see dot_ansible/roles/devtools/
# tasks/main.yml `# --- vhs ---` block.
#
# noRoot=true on Linux: the upstream run_onchange script injects
# `--skip-tags sudo`, which strips the apt block below (it carries
# `tags: [sudo]`). No extra in-role guard needed; user-level fallbacks
# would be impractical for these packages (ffmpeg / imagemagick / libvips
# all want C compilers + system codecs).

# =============================================================================
# macOS — all via Homebrew
# =============================================================================

- name: Install media/AV tools (macOS)
  when: ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Darwin"
  community.general.homebrew:
    name:
      - ffmpeg        # provides ffmpeg, ffprobe, ffplay
      - imagemagick   # v7 unified `magick` binary (also ships `convert` shim)
      - exiftool
      - vips          # provides vips, vipsthumbnail, vipsedit
    state: present

# =============================================================================
# Linux (Debian/Ubuntu) — apt
# =============================================================================

- name: Install media/AV tools from apt (Debian/Ubuntu)
  when: ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Debian"
  become: true
  tags: [sudo]
  ansible.builtin.apt:
    name:
      - ffmpeg                       # ffmpeg + ffprobe + ffplay
      - imagemagick                  # Ubuntu 24.04 ships v6 → /usr/bin/convert
      - libimage-exiftool-perl       # provides /usr/bin/exiftool
      - libvips-tools                # vips, vipsthumbnail, vipsedit
    state: present
    # Don't re-run apt-get update here: these are all main-archive/universe
    # packages already covered by the base role's best-effort cache refresh at
    # play start. An inlined update_cache would let a single transient
    # proxy/source failure abort the whole play (it did on a flaky proxy).
    # See pitfalls/apt-update-fails-base-role-empty-error.md.
    update_cache: false

```text
def parse_args(argv: list[str]) -> argparse.Namespace:
    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="appsrc",
                                description="Detect how an installed app / CLI was installed & managed.")
    sub = p.add_subparsers(dest="cmd")

    ps = sub.add_parser("scan", help="Batch-inventory installed apps + CLIs (cached).")
    ps.add_argument("--json", action="store_true", help="Emit JSON.")
    ps.add_argument("--tsv", action="store_true",
                    help="Emit TSV: name<TAB>source<TAB>path<TAB>kind<TAB>package (for tv / scripts).")
    ps.add_argument("--kind", choices=["gui", "cli", "all"], default="all", help="Restrict inventory.")
    ps.add_argument("--source", default="", help="Filter by source id/label substring.")
    ps.add_argument("--sort", choices=["source", "name", "size"], default="source",
                    help="Sort order (size => biggest first; implies --size).")
    ps.add_argument("-r", "--refresh", action="store_true", help="Recompute; ignore cache.")
    ps.add_argument("--no-cache", action="store_true", help="Don't read or write cache.")
    ps.add_argument("--size", action="store_true",
                    help="Also compute each item's bundle size (slower; mtime-cached).")
    ps.add_argument("--human", action="store_true",
                    help="With --tsv, emit human-readable sizes (e.g. 3.7G) instead of bytes.")
    ps.add_argument("--list-names", action="store_true", help=argparse.SUPPRESS)

    pw = sub.add_parser("which", help="Single lookup (live): command or GUI app name.")
    pw.add_argument("name", nargs="?", default="", help="Command or app name.")
    pw.add_argument("--json", action="store_true", help="Emit JSON.")
    pw.add_argument("--path", default="", help="Classify PATH directly.")

    pz = sub.add_parser("size", help="Footprint + associated storage (cache/data/containers) for one app.")
    pz.add_argument("name", nargs="?", default="", help="Command or app name.")
    pz.add_argument("--json", action="store_true", help="Emit JSON.")
    pz.add_argument("--path", default="", help="Size PATH directly.")

    pt = sub.add_parser("tui", help="Interactive dashboard: sort by size, filter, drill in.")
    pt.add_argument("--kind", choices=["gui", "cli", "all"], default="all", help="Initial inventory.")

    # Default routing: bare `appsrc` / flags → scan; a bare word → `which WORD`.
    if not argv:
        argv = ["scan"]
    elif argv[0] in ("-h", "--help"):
        pass
    elif argv[0] not in ("scan", "which", "size", "tui"):
        argv = (["scan", *argv] if argv[0].startswith("-") else ["which", *argv])
    return p.parse_args(argv)


def _list_names() -> int:
    if IS_MAC:
        for app in _mac_gui_apps():
            print(app.stem)
    elif IS_LINUX:
        for name, _ in _linux_desktop_apps():
            print(name)
    return 0


def main() -> int:
    args = parse_args(sys.argv[1:])
    if getattr(args, "list_names", False):
        return _list_names()
    if args.cmd == "which":
        if not args.name and not args.path:
            err.print("[red]appsrc which: need a NAME or --path.[/red]")
            return 2
        return do_which(args)
    if args.cmd == "size":
        if not args.name and not args.path:
            err.print("[red]appsrc size: need a NAME or --path.[/red]")
            return 2
        return do_size(args)
    if args.cmd == "tui":
        return do_tui(args)
    return do_scan(args)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())
=====DATACLASSES=====
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Record + labels
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
@dataclass
class AppRecord:
    name: str
    kind: str                       # "gui" | "cli"
    path: str | None
    source: str                     # canonical id (see SOURCE_LABELS)
    manager: str | None = None      # human label
    package: str | None = None      # owning cask/formula/deb/snap/crate
    confidence: str = "heuristic"   # "authoritative" | "heuristic"
    bundle_id: str | None = None    # macOS CFBundleIdentifier
    signer: str | None = None       # macOS codesign Authority leaf
    origin_url: str | None = None   # macOS kMDItemWhereFroms
    detail: str | None = None
    mtime: float | None = None
    size_bytes: int | None = None   # bundle footprint; only filled by `scan --size`


@dataclass
class StorageItem:
    category: str                   # bundle|cache|data|container|prefs|state|logs|web|launch|xdg
    path: str
    size_bytes: int | None          # None = unreadable / du timed out
    confidence: str                 # "exact" | "fuzzy"
    note: str | None = None


@dataclass
class SizeReport:
    name: str
    source: str
    kind: str
    path: str | None
    bundle_bytes: int | None
    associated_bytes: int           # sum of non-bundle items
    total_bytes: int
    items: list[StorageItem]


SOURCE_LABELS = {
    "homebrew-cask": "Homebrew cask",
    "homebrew-formula": "Homebrew formula",
    "mac-app-store": "Mac App Store",
    "direct-download-pkg": "Direct download (pkg)",
    "direct-download-dmg": "Direct download (dmg/web)",
    "manual": "Manual / drag-in",
    "macos-system": "macOS system",
    "apt": "apt / dpkg",
    "snap": "snap",
    "flatpak": "flatpak",
    "appimage": "AppImage",
    "linuxbrew": "Homebrew (Linuxbrew)",
    "cargo": "cargo",

#!/usr/bin/env bats

setup() {
  setup_path_stub

teardown() {
  [ -n "${X_TMP:-}" ] && [ -d "$X_TMP" ] && rm -rf "$X_TMP"

_stub_uname() {

#!/usr/bin/env bash
printf '%s\n' "$value"
EOF
  chmod +x "$BATS_STUB_DIR/uname"

=====HELPER=====
# Shared helpers for bats tests. Source from each .bats file:
#   load "../test_helper.bash"   # or the equivalent relative path
#
# Keep this file tiny. No bats-assert / bats-file / bats-support — plain

REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$BATS_TEST_DIRNAME/.." && pwd)"
if [ "$(basename "$REPO_ROOT")" = "tests" ]; then
  REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$REPO_ROOT/.." && pwd)"
fi

_BATS_STUB_DIRS=()

# Create a temp directory and prepend it to PATH. Exposes the path via
# $BATS_STUB_DIR (not via stdout) so the PATH export actually sticks — using
# command substitution would run this in a subshell and discard the export.
setup_path_stub() {
  BATS_STUB_DIR="$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/bats-stub.XXXXXX")"
  _BATS_STUB_DIRS+=("$BATS_STUB_DIR")
  PATH="$BATS_STUB_DIR:$PATH"
  export PATH BATS_STUB_DIR
}

# Cleanup function. Call from your own teardown() if you override it:
#   teardown() { your_cleanup; cleanup_path_stubs; }
cleanup_path_stubs() {
  local dir
  for dir in "${_BATS_STUB_DIRS[@]:-}"; do
    [ -n "$dir" ] && [ -d "$dir" ] && rm -rf "$dir"
  done
  _BATS_STUB_DIRS=()
}

# Default teardown — fires only if the .bats file does not define its own.
teardown() { cleanup_path_stubs; }

**Dynamic candidates wired up:**

- `fleet` host names — `_fleet_hosts_one` / `_fleet_hosts_csv` shell out to `fleet hosts --list`. Used for the positional `fleet hosts NAME`, `fleet chezmoi diff HOST`, `fleet chezmoi tail HOST`, and the `--hosts=foo,bar,baz` CSV flag everywhere.
- `pqsum -g <GROUP>` — `_pqsum` shells out to `pueue status --json | jq '.groups | keys[]'`.
- `mlf` ids (run-id, experiment-id, model-name) — **not** auto-completed (would round-trip MLflow tracking server, possibly auth-required). Use `tv mlflow` for fuzzy id picking instead.
- `yth` video ids — **not** auto-completed (opaque 11-char ids; enumerating the whole history on every TAB is wasteful). Use `tv yth` or `yth search <query>` instead.
- `wake` host names — `_wake` shells out to `wake --list-names` (reads `~/.config/wake/hosts.toml`), same pattern as `_fleet_hosts_one`.
- `appsrc which <name>` / `appsrc size <name>` — `_appsrc_names` shells out to `appsrc scan --list-names` (installed GUI app names) and adds `_command_names -e` / `compgen -c` (PATH commands), so both a GUI app name and a shell command complete. Same shell-out pattern as `_wake` / `_fleet_hosts_one`.
- `herdr-grep --session <name>` — both completion files shell out to `herdr-grep --list-sessions`, which reads the local Herdr session registry and returns sorted running names. Errors are silent so TAB still works when no Herdr server is running.

**Adding a new in-house CLI** (decision flow):

1. **Does it use tyro?** → Use Strategy A. Mirror `dot_config/shell/47_mi_router.sh`. Add a `<tool>-update-completion` helper to `dot_config/shell/10_aliases.sh`. Don't forget to rewrite `#compdef` in zsh post-gen.
2. **Does it use argparse?** → Two sub-options:
   - Add `argcomplete.autocomplete(parser)` to the script + Strategy C cached eval at startup.
   - Hand-write Strategy B completion (smaller / no Python dependency at every shell startup).
3. **Hand-rolled / shell script** → Strategy B hand-written. One zsh file in `dot_config/zsh/tools/<NN>_<name>_completion.zsh`, one bash file in `dot_config/bash/<NN>_<name>_completion.bash`. Mirror `_fleet`'s structure: top-level dispatcher → per-subcommand functions → dynamic helpers.
4. **Update this table + `docs/shells/aliases.md`** in the same commit (per the cross-file maintenance rule in `CLAUDE.md`).

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# chafa wrapper — force `--probe off`.
#
# WHY: yazi's fallback image adapter shells out to `chafa` for terminals with no
# native graphics protocol (e.g. Alacritty) and there is no way to pass it flags.
# chafa >=1.16 probes the terminal for its fg/bg colors via OSC 10/11 queries;
# inside tmux/zellij chafa often exits before the multiplexer delivers the reply,
# so the terminal's `rgb:…` response leaks into yazi's input buffer and pops a
# spurious rename / shell prompt (yazi #3680 — closed "not planned": it's a mux
# leak; chafa's `--probe off` is the source-side cure). `--probe off` only skips
# color auto-detection (chafa falls back to sensible defaults from $TERM/
# $COLORTERM), so ascii-art previews are unchanged.

567:| `ssh-setup-remote` | function | `dot_config/shell/96_ssh_setup.sh` | Interactive wizard: select/create an SSH key, `ssh-copy-id`, then wire it into local `~/.ssh/config` — **edits the existing `Host` block in place** if the alias is already configured (following `Include config.d/*` recursively), else appends a new alias and offers to add a missing `Include`. Needs `python3` for in-place edits; falls back to append-only otherwise. |
750:| `abspath [-r] [-t] [PATH...]` | function | `dot_config/shell/58_abspath.sh` | Print absolute path(s): no args → logical cwd (like `pwd`); `PATH...` → one absolute path per line. Logical by default (normalizes `.`/`..`, keeps symlinks, existence not required); `-r`/`--resolve` → physical path (follows symlinks, must exist); `-t`/`--tilde` → abbreviate a `$HOME`-rooted result to `~`. stdout stays pipe-clean, so `abspath FILE \| x copy` grabs a path to the clipboard (fills the `realpath FILE \| x copy` hint in `x`'s help). Requires python3 |
751:| `cref [-a\|-c] [-L] [-n] [--] FILE[:LINE[-LINE]]` | function | `dot_config/shell/59_cref.sh` | Copy a Cursor/Claude-Code-style file mention (`@path`, `@path:12`, `@path:12-40`) to the clipboard — the shell twin of Neovim's `<leader>y` [copy-reference](../neovim/copy-reference.md) maps. Path flavor: default = **git-root-relative** (falls back to cwd/`~`/absolute the way nvim's `:~:.` does); `-a`/`--absolute` = machine-absolute; `-c`/`--cwd` = relative to `$PWD`. Line info comes from `FILE:LINE[-LINE]`, trailing positionals (`cref FILE 12 40`), or — with no FILE arg — the first stdin line in grep/ripgrep `FILE:LINE:…` format (`rg -n foo \| cref`); a trailing `:col[:text]` is dropped and `:12-12` collapses to `:12`. Copies via the `x` CLI (OSC 52, SSH-safe); `-n`/`--no-copy` prints only, `-L`/`--no-line` forces a bare `@path`. stdout stays pipe-clean; `Copied @…` toast on stderr. Requires python3 |
858:| `yth [ARGS…]` | CLI (bin) | `dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_yth` | Search your YouTube watch history (title/channel/description + captions). #
# crash-blackbox — flight recorder for machines that hard-power-off with no logs.
#
# When a box loses power outright (PSU trip, VRM fault, AGESA reset) the kernel
# never gets to run, so journald's write buffer dies with it and the last ~30s
# of evidence is simply gone. This samples the sensors every second and fsyncs
# each row, so the CSV survives the cut and `report` can show you the seconds

<tool-use data-tool-type="read" data-tool-name="Read"><details>
<summary>Tool use: **Read**</summary>
 `./docs/zsh/zsh-completions.md`

```text
1	# Zsh & Bash Completions
2	
3	How tab completions are organized in this dotfiles project — for both upstream tools and in-house CLIs (`fleet`, `mlf`, `pqsum`, `mi-router`, `x`).
4	
5	## How autocomplete works (mechanics)
6	
7	Tab completion is the same idea on both shells but the plumbing differs.
8	
9	### zsh — `compinit` + `fpath` + autoload `_<tool>` functions
10	
11	1. **`compinit`** scans every directory in `$fpath` for files starting with `_` and registers them as completion candidates. Run by oh-my-zsh once at startup.
12	2. **`$fpath`** is zsh's function search path. Order in this repo (`dot_zshrc.tmpl:67-70`):
13	   ```
14	   ~/.zfunc                                             ← user-generated (this repo's lazy autoload target)
15	   ~/.oh-my-zsh/custom/plugins/zsh-completions/src/     ← community (184 tools)
16	   ~/.docker/completions/                               ← Docker-shipped
17	   $(brew --prefix)/share/zsh/site-functions/           ← Homebrew-managed
18	   ```
19	3. **The first line of each file** matters: `#compdef <name>` tells zsh which command to bind to. If you write `#compdef fleet`, then `fleet<TAB>` invokes the file's `_fleet` function.
20	4. **Autoload vs eager-load**: a file in `$fpath` is *parsed* the first time the user actually TABs the command (lazy). Files sourced explicitly at startup (e.g. via `load_modular_dir` in this repo) call `compdef _<func> <cmd>` directly — parsed eagerly, no need to be in `$fpath`.
21	5. **`_arguments` DSL** (zsh-only) lets you describe options + positional args declaratively: `'--hosts=[help text]:hosts:_fleet_hosts_csv'` defines the flag, hint, and a custom completer function. See `dot_config/zsh/tools/45_fleet_completion.zsh`.
22	
23	### bash — `bash-completion v2` + `complete -F` + `COMPREPLY`
24	
25	1. **bash-completion v2** is sourced at shell startup by `dot_config/bash/03_completion.bash`. It auto-loads completion files on first TAB.
26	2. **The user dir** is `${XDG_DATA_HOME:-~/.local/share}/bash-completion/completions/` — drop a file named after the command (e.g. `mi-router`) here and v2 lazy-loads it on TAB.
27	3. **`complete -F _func cmd`** registers a bash function as the completer for `cmd`. The function reads `$COMP_WORDS` / `$COMP_CWORD` and writes candidates to `$COMPREPLY`.
28	4. **`_init_completion` + `compgen`** are bash-completion v2 helpers — `_init_completion` populates `cur`/`prev`/`words`/`cword`; `compgen -W "list" -- "$cur"` filters a wordlist by the current prefix.
29	5. **Eager vs lazy** mirrors zsh: a file in the user dir is lazy; a file sourced via `load_modular_dir` (this repo's `dot_config/bash/`) calls `complete -F` immediately.
30	
31	### Three generation strategies in this repo
32	
33	| Strategy | Where the file lives | Trigger | Best for |
34	|---|---|---|---|
35	| **A. Lazy autoload** | zsh `~/.zfunc/_<tool>` / bash `${XDG_DATA_HOME}/bash-completion/completions/<tool>` | First TAB on the command | Tools that ship `--print-completion <shell>` or similar (tyro, click, clap-derive — including this repo's `mi-router`) |
36	| **B. Eager-load at startup** | `dot_config/zsh/tools/<NN>_<tool>_completion.zsh` + `dot_config/bash/<NN>_<tool>_completion.bash` | Sourced via `load_modular_dir` after compinit / bash-completion v2 init | Hand-written completion (this repo's `fleet`, `mlf`, `pqsum`, `x`) |
37	| **C. Cached eval at startup** | `${XDG_CACHE_HOME}/<shell>/<tool>_completion.<ext>` | Sourced via shell `init` script (`dot_config/shell/<NN>_<tool>.sh`) | Slow generators whose output has side effects beyond `compdef` (e.g. `thefuck --alias` outputs an `alias` line — needs to land in the running shell's namespace, not just a deferred `_<tool>` function) |
38	
39	Cache invalidation in classes A and C uses **binary-mtime check**:
40	```sh
41	[ ! -f "$cache" ] || [ "$(command -v <tool>)" -nt "$cache" ]  # → regenerate
42	```
43	This catches `brew upgrade`, `uv tool upgrade`, `mise install <NEW>` — anything that bumps the binary's mtime. Manual `<tool>-update-completion` helpers (in `dot_config/{shell,zsh}/10_aliases.zsh`) cover edge cases (gem-only upgrades, in-place replacements, cache corruption).
44	
45	## Architecture
46	
47	```
48	compinit runs once (inside oh-my-zsh.sh)
49	        │
50	        ├── ~/.zfunc/                          ← user-generated completions (NOT tracked by chezmoi)
51	        ├── ~/.oh-my-zsh/custom/plugins/       ← community completions (184 files, cloned by ansible)
52	        │     └── zsh-completions/src/
53	        ├── ~/.docker/completions/             ← Docker-shipped completions
54	        ├── $(brew --prefix)/share/zsh/        ← Homebrew-managed completions (via `brew completions link`)
55	        │     └── site-functions/
56	        └── $ZSH/completions/                  ← oh-my-zsh built-in completions
57	```
58	
59	All `fpath` additions are in `dot_zshrc.tmpl` **before** `source "$ZSH/oh-my-zsh.sh"`, so `compinit` runs exactly once and picks up everything.
60	
61	## Completion Categories
62	
63	Tools fall into four categories:
64	
65	### A. Self-generating (`tool completion zsh > ~/.zfunc/_tool`)
66	
67	Most modern CLI tools can output their own completion script. **Auto-generated for both shells** by the `chezmoi apply` hook (`run_after_50_generate_completions.sh.tmpl` → `scripts/generate_completions.sh`); see [Generating Completions After Fresh Install](#generating-completions-after-fresh-install) for opt-out + manual rerun.
68	
69	| Tool | Command |
70	|------|---------|
71	| `uv` | `uv generate-shell-completion zsh` |
72	| `mise` | `mise completion zsh` |
73	| `chezmoi` | `chezmoi completion zsh` |
74	| `just` | `just --completions zsh` |
75	| `bat` | `bat --completion zsh` |
76	| `delta` | `delta --generate-completion zsh` |
77	| `starship` | `starship completions zsh` |
78	| `rg` | `rg --generate complete-zsh` |
79	| `fd` | `fd --gen-completions zsh` |
80	| `zellij` | `zellij setup --generate-completion zsh` |
81	| `sesh` | `sesh completion zsh` |
82	| `pueue` | `pueue completions zsh` |
83	| `docker` | `docker completion zsh` |
84	| `gh` | `gh completion -s zsh` |
85	| `opencode` | `opencode completion zsh` |
86	| `bw` | `bw completion --shell zsh` |
87	
88	**Usage pattern:**
89	
90	```bash
91	# Generate once (or after upgrade)
92	mkdir -p ~/.zfunc
93	uv generate-shell-completion zsh > ~/.zfunc/_uv
94	mise completion zsh > ~/.zfunc/_mise
95	```
96	
97	### B. Pre-bundled (no action needed)
98	
99	Completions ship with the package or via the `zsh-completions` community plugin.
100	
101	| Tool | Source |
102	|------|--------|
103	| `eza` | Homebrew formula installs `_eza` into site-functions |
104	| `git` | oh-my-zsh `git` plugin |
105	| `yazi` | Ships `_yazi` in release assets (also in zsh-completions) |
106	| `lazygit` | No completion support; not needed (TUI app) |
107	| `btop` | No completion support; not needed (TUI app) |
108	| Many others | `zsh-completions` plugin covers 184 tools |
109	
110	### C. Eval/source at startup (shell integration)
111	
112	These tools inject completions as part of broader shell integration. Most live in the POSIX `dot_config/shell/` layer (sourced by both zsh and bash); zsh-only ones live in `dot_config/zsh/tools/`.
113	
114	| Tool | Where | How | Cached? |
115	|------|-------|-----|---------|
116	| `fzf` | `dot_config/shell/10_fzf.sh` | `eval "$(fzf --zsh)"` (zsh) / `eval "$(fzf --bash)"` (bash) | — |
117	| `zoxide` | `dot_config/shell/20_zoxide.sh` | `eval "$(zoxide init <shell>)"` | — |
118	| `direnv` | `dot_config/shell/30_direnv.sh` | `eval "$(direnv hook <shell>)"` | — |
119	| `marimo` | `dot_config/shell/29_marimo.sh` | `_MARIMO_COMPLETE=<shell>_source marimo` | ✅ `${XDG_CACHE_HOME}/{zsh,bash}/marimo_completion.{zsh,bash}` — refresh via `marimo-update-completion` |
120	| `thefuck` | `dot_config/shell/27_thefuck.sh` | `thefuck --alias` | ✅ `${XDG_CACHE_HOME}/{zsh,bash}/thefuck_alias.{zsh,bash}` — refresh via `thefuck-update-completion` |
121	| `try-cli` | `dot_config/zsh/tools/32_try.zsh` | `ruby try.rb init` (zsh-only) | ✅ `${XDG_CACHE_HOME}/zsh/try_init.zsh` — refresh via `try-update-completion` |
122	
123	> **Cached entries** auto-invalidate when the tool's binary mtime is newer than the cache file (`[ "$(command -v <tool>)" -nt "$cache" ]`) — catches `mise install <NEW>`, `brew upgrade`, `uv tool upgrade`. Manual refresh helpers handle edge cases: gem-only upgrades that don't bump the ruby binary, in-place tool replacements, or cache corruption. The pattern mirrors `dot_config/zsh/tools/95_bitwarden.zsh` (the canonical example).
124	
125	### D. No completion support
126	
127	`claude`, `gemini`, `agy`/`agyc` (Antigravity CLI), `btop`, `lazygit` -- no generation command available.
128	
129	### E. Python tools via `shtab` / `tyro` / `click` / `argcomplete`
130	
131	Python CLI frameworks can generate completions. Pick by what your script uses:
132	
133	- **[tyro](https://brentyi.github.io/tyro/tab_completion/)** (this repo's `mi-router` + every `scripts/fleet/*.py` and `scripts/mlf/*.py` subcommand): `<tool> --tyro-write-completion zsh <path>`. Native flag — auto-added when you call `tyro.cli(...)`. tyro emits `#compdef <full-binary-path>` for zsh, so post-process the first line to the short name (see `dot_config/shell/47_mi_router.sh` for the canonical pattern). Bash output already binds `basename`, no fixup needed.
134	- **[shtab](https://github.com/iterative/shtab)**: `shtab --shell=zsh my_module.parser > ~/.zfunc/_my_tool`. Decorate-an-`argparse.ArgumentParser` style; works for both shells.
135	- **argcomplete**: `register-python-argcomplete tool_name` (eval-at-startup style, category C). Requires the script to call `argcomplete.autocomplete(parser)` before `parse_args()`. Cross-shell.

169	- `yth` video ids — **not** auto-completed (opaque 11-char ids; enumerating the whole history on every TAB is wasteful). Use `tv yth` or `yth search <query>` instead.
170	- `wake` host names — `_wake` shells out to `wake --list-names` (reads `~/.config/wake/hosts.toml`), same pattern as `_fleet_hosts_one`.
171	- `appsrc which <name>` / `appsrc size <name>` — `_appsrc_names` shells out to `appsrc scan --list-names` (installed GUI app names) and adds `_command_names -e` / `compgen -c` (PATH commands), so both a GUI app name and a shell command complete. Same shell-out pattern as `_wake` / `_fleet_hosts_one`.
172	- `herdr-grep --session <name>` — both completion files shell out to `herdr-grep --list-sessions`, which reads the local Herdr session registry and returns sorted running names. Errors are silent so TAB still works when no Herdr server is running.

174	**Adding a new in-house CLI** (decision flow):
175	
176	1. **Does it use tyro?** → Use Strategy A. Mirror `dot_config/shell/47_mi_router.sh`. Add a `<tool>-update-completion` helper to `dot_config/shell/10_aliases.sh`. Don't forget to rewrite `#compdef` in zsh post-gen.
177	2. **Does it use argparse?** → Two sub-options:
178	   - Add `argcomplete.autocomplete(parser)` to the script + Strategy C cached eval at startup.
179	   - Hand-write Strategy B completion (smaller / no Python dependency at every shell startup).
180	3. **Hand-rolled / shell script** → Strategy B hand-written. One zsh file in `dot_config/zsh/tools/<NN>_<name>_completion.zsh`, one bash file in `dot_config/bash/<NN>_<name>_completion.bash`. Mirror `_fleet`'s structure: top-level dispatcher → per-subcommand functions → dynamic helpers.
181	4. **Update this table + `docs/shells/aliases.md`** in the same commit (per the cross-file maintenance rule in `CLAUDE.md`).
182	
183	## Why `~/.zfunc/` is NOT Tracked by Chezmoi
184	
185	**Decision: `~/.zfunc/` is not version-controlled.** Rationale:
186	
187	1. **Completions are tool-version-dependent.** A completion script generated by `uv 0.6` may not match `uv 0.7`. Tracking stale files causes subtle breakage.
188	2. **Not all users install the same tools.** A `_pueue` completion file is useless (and throws warnings) if pueue isn't installed.
189	3. **Regeneration is trivial.** One command per tool.
190	4. **Brew-installed tools auto-manage their completions** via site-functions. Duplicating them in `~/.zfunc/` creates conflicts.
191	
192	### What we DO track
193	
194	- `fpath+=~/.zfunc` in `dot_zshrc.tmpl` (ensures the directory is in the search path)
195	- `zsh-completions` plugin cloned by ansible (community completions)
196	- `~/.docker/completions` fpath entry
197	- Tool-specific `eval`/`source` integrations in `dot_config/zsh/tools/`
198	
199	## Generating Completions After Fresh Install
200	
201	**Automatic — no manual step needed.** Every `chezmoi apply` runs `.chezmoiscripts/global/run_after_50_generate_completions.sh.tmpl`, which calls `scripts/generate_completions.sh` and regenerates completion for the 14 self-generating tools listed in Section A (`chezmoi`, `mise`, `uv`, `just`, `starship`, `gh`, `docker`, `rg`, `fd`, `bat`, `delta`, `zellij`, `pueue`, `opencode`).
202	
203	The hook is **idempotent** — it stat-checks each tool's binary mtime against the existing completion file and skips if the cache is fresh. Cost when nothing changed: **~21ms** total (presence checks + 28 stat calls). After an `ansible-playbook` / `brew upgrade` / `mise install <NEW>` that bumps a binary's mtime: ~140ms one-shot to regenerate the affected completions.
204	
205	Output paths:
206	- **zsh**: `~/.zfunc/_<tool>` — lazy-loaded by compinit on first TAB (in `$fpath` via `dot_zshrc.tmpl:68`).
207	- **bash**: `${XDG_DATA_HOME:-~/.local/share}/bash-completion/completions/<tool>` — lazy-loaded by bash-completion v2 on first TAB.
208	
209	### Manual rerun
210	
211	```bash
212	just completions-refresh                              # force regen all (--force)
213	bash scripts/generate_completions.sh --force          # same, no `just`
214	bash scripts/generate_completions.sh                  # mtime-checked (same as the chezmoi hook)
215	```
216	
217	Use `just completions-refresh` after a tool upgrade outside the chezmoi flow (e.g. `cargo install <tool>`), or to recover from a corrupted completion file.
218	
219	### Opt out
220	
221	```bash
222	export CHEZMOI_SKIP_COMPLETION_GEN=1   # in ~/.shellrc.adhoc; suppresses the chezmoi-apply hook
223	```
224	
225	Existing completion files stay as-is; you can still run `just completions-refresh` manually.
226	
227	### Add a new tool to the auto-gen inventory
228	
229	Edit the `regen <tool> "<zsh-args>" "<bash-args>"` block in `scripts/generate_completions.sh`. The arguments are whatever follows the tool name to produce the per-shell completion script — check `<tool> completion --help` or `<tool> --help | grep -i complet`. Examples already in the script cover click (`_TOOL_COMPLETE=`), clap (`--generate complete-<shell>`), tyro (`--tyro-write-completion <shell>`-equivalent), cobra (`completion <shell>`), and ad-hoc styles (`--completions <shell>`).
230	
231	### What about tools NOT in the auto-gen inventory?
232	
233	- **`sesh` / `tv` / `worktrunk`**: shell-startup mtime check (each tool has its own `dot_config/zsh/tools/<NN>_<tool>.zsh` file that runs the version check on every shell start — these tools are typically `cargo install`-ed outside chezmoi, so they need the per-startup probe to catch user upgrades).
234	- **`bw` / `marimo` / `thefuck` / `try-cli`**: cached eval at startup (their completion script has side effects beyond `compdef`, so the file is `source`'d into the running shell rather than autoloaded).
235	- **`mi-router`**: tyro self-gen, lives in `dot_config/shell/47_mi_router.sh` (not the bulk script — has its own `#compdef` rewrite for tyro's full-path output quirk).
236	- **`fleet` / `mlf` / `pqsum` / `x` / `dotcfg` / `agent-warmup`**: hand-written completion in `dot_config/{zsh/tools,bash}/45-54_*_completion.*` (in-house CLIs without a built-in completion generator). `dotcfg`'s `--set` key list mirrors the PROMPTS table in `scripts/init/dotfiles_init.py`.
237	
238	## Priority / Override Order
239	
240	When the same `_tool` file exists in multiple fpath directories, the **first match wins**:
241	
242	```
243	1. ~/.zfunc/                                    (highest - your overrides)
244	2. ~/.oh-my-zsh/custom/plugins/zsh-completions/src/
245	3. ~/.docker/completions/
246	4. $(brew --prefix)/share/zsh/site-functions/   (Homebrew-managed)
247	5. /usr/share/zsh/*/functions/                  (system, lowest)
248	```
249	
250	Current `dot_zshrc.tmpl` order:
251	
252	```zsh
253	fpath+=~/.zfunc                     # appended (lowest of custom)
254	fpath=(zsh-completions/src $fpath)  # prepended (higher than ~/.zfunc)
255	fpath=(~/.docker/completions $fpath) # prepended (highest of custom)
256	```
257	
258	If you want `~/.zfunc/` to override community completions, change to prepend:
259	
260	```zsh
261	fpath=(~/.zfunc $fpath)  # prepend instead of append
262	```
263	
264	## FAQ
265	
266	**Q: Should I generate completions for tools that `zsh-completions` already covers?**
267	A: Only if you want the latest version. The community plugin may lag behind. For fast-moving tools (uv, mise), generating your own is worthwhile.
268	
269	**Q: A completion file throws errors after I uninstall a tool. What do I do?**
270	A: Remove the file: `rm ~/.zfunc/_toolname`. Stale `_tool` files in fpath are harmless (silently ignored) unless they have syntax errors.
271	
272	**Q: How do I debug completion issues?**
273	A: Run `echo $fpath | tr ' ' '\n'` to see all fpath entries. Use `which _toolname` to see which completion file is being used. Force rebuild with `rm -f ~/.zcompdump && compinit`.
274
