## C. The player-compatibility profile system

### Where profiles live

- **Built-ins**: a frozen dict in `scripts/ytmv/profile.py` (singular — the *leaf* module is `profiles.py`; keeping the names distinct avoids a self-import collision).
- **User-extensible**: `[profiles.<name>]` tables in `~/.config/ytmv/config.toml`, each with an optional `inherits = "safe"`. A user table with an existing built-in name **overrides** it (so the user can retune `safe` without renaming).
- **Scalar defaults**: `[defaults]` in the same file, applied on top of the profile.

### Resolution order (later wins)

1. Built-in `PROFILES["safe"]` — the floor, so a profile table is never required to be complete.
2. `inherits` chain (built-in or user, cycle-detected, max depth 5).
3. The selected profile's own keys.
4. `[defaults]` scalar keys from config.toml.
5. CLI flags that are not `None`/`""`.

Selection: `--profile NAME` > `$YTMV_PROFILE` > `[defaults].profile` in config.toml > `"safe"`.

`resolve_profile(name, cfg, overrides) -> Profile` is a **pure function returning a frozen dataclass**. This is the single most valuable offline test target in the whole CLI.

### The settings


### The five built-ins

| | `safe` **(default)** | `cjk-big5` | `cjk-gbk` | `ipod` | `modern` |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| target | unknown generic player | Traditional-Chinese firmware | Simplified-Chinese firmware | iPod Classic/Nano | phone / Rockbox / VLC |
| `id3_version` | 3 | 3 | 3 | 3 | 4 |
| `id3_encoding` | utf-16 | utf-16 | utf-16 | utf-16 | utf-8 |
| `id3v1` | true | true | true | false | false |
| `strip_unknown_frames` | true | true | true | true | false |
| `uslt` / `sylt` | on / **off** | on / off | on / off | on / off | on / **on** |
| `sidecar_lrc` | on | on | on | off | on |
| `lrc_encoding` | utf-8 | **cp950** | **cp936** | utf-8 | utf-8 |
| `lrc_newline` | crlf | crlf | crlf | lf | lf |
| `on_unencodable` | warn-replace | warn-replace | warn-replace | warn-replace | utf8 |
| `plain_txt_sidecar` | false | true | true | false | false |
| `mp3_bitrate` / vbr | 192 / no | 192 / no | 192 / no | 256 / no | 320 / yes |
| `cover` / max px / fmt | on / 300 / jpeg | on / 300 / jpeg | on / 300 / jpeg | on / 300 / jpeg | on / 1000 / jpeg |
| `cover_sidecar` | true | true | true | false | false |
| `video_max_height` | 320 | 320 | 320 | 480 | 720 |
| `h264 profile/level` | baseline/3.0 | baseline/3.0 | baseline/3.0 | baseline/3.0 | high/4.0 |
| `softsub` / `hardsub` | off / **on** | off / on | off / on | off / on | **on** / off |
| `filename_style` | fat32 | fat32 | fat32 | fat32 | loose |
| `filename_max_len` | 64 | 64 | 64 | 120 | 200 |

Rationale for the two non-obvious defaults:

- **`safe` burns subtitles rather than muxing soft subs.** A player old enough to need ID3v2.3+UTF-16 will not render mov_text. Burn-in is the only delivery that is *guaranteed* to show up on unknown hardware. (This is why the libass gap in §E is a blocking prerequisite for the default profile, not a nice-to-have.)
- **`sylt` off everywhere except `modern`.** SYLT is spec'd but essentially unimplemented outside a handful of players, and a malformed SYLT frame is a realistic way to make a fragile 2007 parser skip the whole tag. Ship it, don't default it.

**Encoding names:** the profile is *named* `cjk-big5` but the codec is **`cp950`**, and `cjk-gbk` uses **`cp936`**. Player firmware and Windows-derived toolchains implement the MS supersets, not the bare standards; Python's `big5`/`gb2312` will raise `UnicodeEncodeError` on characters that a real player renders fine. Flagged in §K for your sign-off.

---

## D. The download / convert pipeline

### D.1 yt-dlp: Python API, not the binary

**Use `yt_dlp.YoutubeDL` (the PEP-723 dep), exactly as `scripts/yth/fetch_subs.py:80-104` does.** Four reasons:

1. We need `extract_info(url, download=False)` to read `artist`/`track`/`album`/`release_year`/`duration`/`thumbnails` **before** choosing filenames, profile-driven sanitisation, and the LRCLIB query. Shelling out means either a second process or parsing `--print-json`.
2. Errors arrive as typed exceptions (`yt_dlp.utils.DownloadError`, `ExtractorError`), which we must classify bot-check-vs-permanent the way `yth enrich` does. Parsing that out of a subprocess's stderr is fragile.
3. The PEP-723 pin makes the version reproducible per-script; the PATH binary drifts independently with ansible runs.
4. Repo precedent, which is worth more than any of the above.

**Documented caveat**: the `~/.local/bin/yt-dlp` installed by `dot_ansible/roles/python_uv_tools/defaults/main.yml:99-105` is **not** what runs. `ytmv doctor` prints both versions side by side so that when YouTube breaks an extractor the user knows which one to bump (`uv cache clean` / drop the `uv` script cache vs `uv tool upgrade yt-dlp`). Same dual-install situation `docs/tools/yth.md:18-19` already documents.

### D.2 Metadata resolution chain

`scripts/ytmv/meta.py::derive(info, overrides) -> TrackMeta` with a `confidence` field (`"explicit" | "structured" | "parsed" | "guess"`):

1. **explicit** — `--artist` / `--track` / `--album` flags.
2. **structured** — `info["artist"]` (or `info["artists"][0]`), `info["track"]`, `info["album"]`, `info["release_year"]`. Present for YouTube's music-metadata videos.
3. **structured (weak)** — `info["creator"]` / `info["composer"]` as artist.
4. **parsed** — clean `info["title"]` then split. Cleaning removes, case-insensitively: parenthesised/bracketed `official (music )?video|official audio|mv|m/v|lyrics?|lyric video|audio|hd|4k|live|full version`, CJK bracket forms `【…】`/`《…》` when they contain those markers, and trailing `| Channel`. Then split on the **first** of ` - `, ` – `, ` — `, `｜`, `//`. Left = artist, right = track. `feat./ft./featuring` in the track is preserved in the tag but stripped from the LRCLIB query.
5. **guess** — artist = `info["uploader"]` with a trailing `" - Topic"` removed (YouTube Music's auto-generated artist channels), track = the cleaned title.

`confidence` drives behaviour: `"guess"` **skips the `/api/get` exact call entirely** (an exact query built from a guess produces confident-looking wrong matches) and auto-enables `--pick` when on a TTY.

### D.3 Tagging: **mutagen owns MP3, yt-dlp/ffmpeg own MP4**

Your instinct is right; here is the confirmation and the precise split.

**MP3 — mutagen owns everything. yt-dlp's embedding post-processors are explicitly disabled.** `FFmpegMetadataPP` routes tags through ffmpeg's id3v2 muxer, which gives no control over per-frame text encoding, cannot write USLT with a chosen encoding, cannot write SYLT at all, and cannot be told to emit v2.3 with UTF-16 while also writing a v1 tail. `EmbedThumbnailPP` would embed the raw 1280×720 WebP/PNG thumbnail as APIC — the single most likely thing to make a 2008 player refuse the file. So the audio `postprocessors` list contains **only** `FFmpegExtractAudio`; `writethumbnail: True` drops the cover to a sidecar for us to process. Any double-write risk is eliminated by never enabling `addmetadata`/`embedthumbnail`.

mutagen writes: `TIT2`, `TPE1`, `TALB`, `TDRC`(v4)/`TYER`(v3), `TRCK`, `TCON`, `COMM` (source URL), `APIC` (type 3, front cover), `USLT` (lang `xxx` or the detected lyric language, empty desc — that's what players look for), optional `SYLT` (type 1 = lyrics, timestamp format 2 = milliseconds), then `tags.save(path, v2_version=profile.id3_version, v1=(2 if profile.id3v1 else 0))`. With `id3_version=3`, mutagen auto-downgrades v4-only frames; we additionally pre-strip them ourselves when `strip_unknown_frames` is on, rather than relying on the downgrade being lossless.

**MP4 — leave it to yt-dlp/ffmpeg.** `embedsubtitles: True` produces mov_text in mp4, which is exactly the correct soft-sub form; `addmetadata: True` writes mp4 atoms, which carry no ID3-compat risk. mutagen is not involved.

### D.4 The four output modes, step by step

Common preamble per URL: `extract_info(download=False)` → `derive()` → `resolve_profile()` → `build_paths()` → skip-existing check → lyric acquisition (§F) → download.

Everything downloads into a `TemporaryDirectory` and is `os.replace`d into place only after tagging succeeds. A Ctrl-C therefore never leaves a half-tagged MP3 that the skip-existing logic would later honour.

**(a) + (b) MP3 (`--mode audio`)** — same media, two lyric deliveries:

```python
opts = {
  "format": "bestaudio/best",
  "outtmpl": f"{tmp}/media.%(ext)s",
  "writethumbnail": profile.cover,
  "postprocessors": [{"key": "FFmpegExtractAudio",
                      "preferredcodec": "mp3",
                      "preferredquality": str(profile.mp3_bitrate)}],
  "postprocessor_args": {"extractaudio+ffmpeg_o":
      ["-ar", str(profile.mp3_samplerate), "-ac", str(profile.mp3_channels),
       *(["-b:a", f"{profile.mp3_bitrate}k"] if not profile.mp3_vbr else [])]},
  "ffmpeg_location": ffmpeg_dir,
  "continuedl": True, "quiet": True, "no_warnings": True,
  **cookie_opts,
}
```

Then, in order: cover prep → mutagen tag write → `.lrc` sidecar write (profile encoding + newline) → optional `folder.jpg` / `.txt` sidecar → atomic move.

**(c) MP4 soft subs (`--mode video --lyrics-out softsub`)**:

```python
"format": f"bv*[height<=?{H}][vcodec^=avc1]+ba[ext=m4a]/b[height<=?{H}]/b",
"merge_output_format": "mp4",
"postprocessors": [{"key": "FFmpegEmbedSubtitle"}, {"key": "FFmpegMetadata"}],
```

We hand yt-dlp our own subtitle file rather than letting it fetch one: write the LRC-derived SRT to `{tmp}/media.zh-Hant.srt` before the download so `FFmpegEmbedSubtitle` picks it up, or (more robust, and what I recommend) skip the post-processor and run the mux ourselves:

```
ffmpeg -y -i media.mp4 -i subs.srt -map 0 -map 1 -c copy -c:s mov_text \
       -metadata:s:s:0 language=zho out.mp4
```

Explicit is better here — `FFmpegEmbedSubtitle`'s file-discovery is filename-convention-driven and silently no-ops when the convention doesn't match.

**(d) MP4 hardsub (`--lyrics-out hardsub`)** — §E.

**Both `--mode audio --mode video` (and `--everything`): download once.** Fetch `bv*+ba` merged, then extract the audio locally:

```
ffmpeg -y -i media.mp4 -vn -c:a libmp3lame -b:a 192k -ar 44100 -ac 2 audio.mp3
```

The `ba` half of the merge *is* bestaudio, so this is not a quality compromise, and it guarantees the MP3 and the MP4 come from the same source. `--separate-audio` forces two downloads for anyone who disagrees.

### D.5 Cover art without ImageMagick

ffmpeg alone, since `installMediaTools` gates both anyway:

```
ffmpeg -y -i cover.webp -vf "scale='min(300,iw)':-2:force_original_aspect_ratio=decrease" \
       -frames:v 1 -q:v 3 cover.jpg
```

If ffmpeg is missing, cover embedding is skipped with one stderr warning — **but note MP3 output is impossible without ffmpeg anyway** (yt-dlp cannot transcode to MP3 without it). So the real dependency statement is: `get` requires ffmpeg, full stop; `lyrics`/`tag`/`search`/`profiles` do not. `docs/tools/ytmv.md` states `installMediaTools=true` as a prerequisite in the same shape as `docs/tools/yth.md:20-21`.

## E. The hardsub problem

### E.1 Runtime probe

`scripts/ytmv/__init__.py::ffmpeg_caps(path) -> dict`:

```python
out = subprocess.run([path, "-hide_banner", "-filters"],
                     capture_output=True, text=True, check=False, timeout=10)
# each line: " ... subtitles         V->V       Render text subtitles ..."
names = {ln.split()[1] for ln in out.stdout.splitlines() if len(ln.split()) > 2}
caps = {"subtitles": "subtitles" in names, "ass": "ass" in names}
```

`-filters` is authoritative (it reflects registered filters); `-buildconf | grep -- --enable-libass` is recorded as a secondary diagnostic only. `libx264` comes from `-hide_banner -encoders`. Results are cached in `cache_dir()/ffmpeg-caps.json` keyed by `(realpath, st_mtime, st_size)`, so a 40-track playlist pays the ~80 ms probe once.

### E.2 Binary selection

Resolution order:

1. `--ffmpeg PATH`
2. `$YTMV_FFMPEG`
3. `ffmpeg = "…"` in `~/.config/ytmv/config.toml`
4. `shutil.which("ffmpeg")` — **if it has the `subtitles` filter**
5. Autodiscovery scan, first hit with `subtitles`:
   `/opt/homebrew/opt/{ffmpeg-full,ffmpeg@7,ffmpeg@6}/bin/ffmpeg`, the `/usr/local/opt/…` equivalents, `/usr/bin/ffmpeg`, `/snap/bin/ffmpeg`
6. Fall back to the PATH ffmpeg for everything *except* burn-in.

The chosen binary is passed to yt-dlp as `ffmpeg_location`, so the whole run is internally consistent. `ytmv doctor` prints the full table (path, version, libass?, libx264?, chosen-for-what).

### E.3 Failure behaviour

- **Explicit `--lyrics-out hardsub`** → **hard fail, exit 3** (broken environment, per the repo's code convention). Silently downgrading to soft subs would hand the user an artifact that does not solve the problem hardsub exists to solve.
- **Implicit via `--everything`** → warn loudly, skip that one artifact, keep the other three, exit 0. `--everything` is a "give me what you can" verb.
- **`--burn-fallback {fail,softsub,skip}`** overrides both (defaults: `fail` explicit, `skip` implicit).

Error text:

```
ytmv get: burned-in subtitles need an ffmpeg built with libass, but
  /opt/homebrew/bin/ffmpeg (8.1.1) has no `subtitles` filter —
  homebrew/core's ffmpeg 8.x dropped libass.
  Fix (pick one):
    brew install ffmpeg@7      # keg-only, won't shadow ffmpeg on PATH
    brew install ffmpeg-full   # everything, large
  ytmv autodetects both. Or point it at a specific build:
    ytmv get … --ffmpeg /path/to/ffmpeg
    ffmpeg = "/opt/homebrew/opt/ffmpeg@7/bin/ffmpeg"   # ~/.config/ytmv/config.toml
  Or produce soft subs instead:  --lyrics-out softsub
  Full probe:  ytmv doctor
```

### E.4 Ansible

Add `ffmpeg@7` to the macOS Homebrew list in `dot_ansible/roles/media_tools/tasks/main.yml` (the block at `# Install media/AV tools (macOS)`), with an inline comment saying it exists solely because homebrew/core `ffmpeg` 8.x dropped libass and `ytmv --lyrics-out hardsub` needs it. This is **inside the already-`installMediaTools`-gated role**, which is permitted; promoting anything ffmpeg-shaped into `devtools` is not, per the `CLAUDE.md:26` hard rule. `ffmpeg@7` is keg-only, so it will not shadow `ffmpeg` on PATH — ytmv finds it by explicit path. Linux needs no change (distro ffmpeg has libass). Flagged in §K because it costs a large bottle/build.

### E.5 LRC → SRT

`scripts/ytmv/lrc.py` — the highest-value pure-function test target after profile resolution.

Parsing (`parse_lrc(text) -> (meta: dict, lines: list[LrcLine])`):
- Tag lines `[ar:…] [ti:…] [al:…] [by:…] [offset:…] [length:…] [re:…] [ve:…]` → `meta`, not cues.
- Timestamp `[mm:ss.xx]` and `[mm:ss.xxx]` and `[mm:ss]` all accepted; `mm` may exceed 59.
- **Repeated timestamps on one line** (`[00:12.00][01:30.00]same text`) expand to N cues.
- Sort by time, drop exact duplicates, drop cues whose text is empty after stripping (they're gaps, not cues).
- `[offset:±N]` in ms: the de-facto convention is *positive shifts lyrics earlier*, i.e. `t_effective = t - offset/1000`. Applied by default; `--ignore-lrc-offset` disables. Documented explicitly because implementations disagree.

Conversion (`lrc_to_srt(lines, track_duration, max_dur=8.0) -> str`):
- `end[i] = min(start[i+1], start[i] + max_dur)`
- `end[last] = min(start[last] + max_dur, track_duration or start[last] + max_dur)`
- Guard `end > start` (if two cues share a timestamp after offset rounding, force `end = start + 0.5`).
- Output `HH:MM:SS,mmm`, blank-line separated, 1-based indices, `\n` newlines (SRT for ffmpeg, not for the player — the *player-facing* sidecar SRT gets the profile's newline and encoding).

`max_dur` default 8 s: without it, the gap before a long instrumental break leaves the previous line burned on screen for a minute.

### E.6 The burn command

libass renders SRT natively (it converts internally), so **we do not hand-write ASS** — we write SRT and use `force_style`:

```
ffmpeg -y -i media.mp4 \
  -vf "subtitles=subs.srt:force_style='FontName=PingFang SC,FontSize=22,Outline=2,Shadow=0,MarginV=30,PrimaryColour=&H00FFFFFF,OutlineColour=&H00000000'" \
  -c:v libx264 -profile:v baseline -level 3.0 -pix_fmt yuv420p -crf 23 \
  -vf-scale-applied-here -c:a aac -b:a 128k -movflags +faststart out.mp4
```

(height cap folded into the same `-vf` chain as `scale=-2:320,subtitles=…`).

**Escaping**: the `subtitles=` filter argument needs `:`, `\`, `'`, `[`, `]`, `,` escaped, and getting that wrong on a path like `~/Music/ytmv/周杰倫 - 稻香.srt` is the classic failure. **Sidestep it entirely**: copy the SRT into the temp dir as plain ASCII `subs.srt` and run ffmpeg with `cwd=tmpdir`, passing the bare relative filename. No escaping needed, ever.

**Font**: `hardsub_font` empty → auto-detect. macOS: `PingFang SC` (always present). Linux: probe `fc-list :lang=zh family` and take the first of `Noto Sans CJK SC` / `Source Han Sans` / `WenQuanYi`. If nothing CJK-capable is found and the lyrics contain non-Latin characters, warn — libass will render tofu boxes and the user needs to know *before* a 5-minute encode.

## F. LRCLIB integration

### HTTP client: **stdlib `urllib.request`**, not `httpx`

`httpx` earns its place in `executable_reyee` / `executable_mi-router` / `executable_tsnet` because those do cookie jars, redirect control, `trust_env=False` proxy suppression (`executable_reyee:173-175`), and TLS quirks. LRCLIB is two unauthenticated GETs with query params returning JSON. Adding a sixth PEP-723 dependency for ~30 lines of `urlopen` is not worth the resolve cost, especially in a script that already pulls `yt-dlp`. Use `urllib.request` with:

- `User-Agent: ytmv/<version> (https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles)` — LRCLIB's docs ask for an identifying UA.
- 10 s timeout; `URLError` / `HTTPError` / `TimeoutError` / `json.JSONDecodeError` are **soft** failures — log to stderr, fall through the chain, never raise.
- No proxy trickery; LRCLIB is a public internet host, so inheriting the environment proxy is correct here (the opposite of the LAN-router case).

### Lookup chain

1. **Skip if `confidence == "guess"`.** Otherwise `GET /api/get?artist_name=&track_name=&duration=` — **album omitted**, because YouTube-derived album names are wrong far more often than they're right and a wrong album turns a hit into a 404. `duration` is the video duration; LRCLIB matches ±2 s server-side.
2. `GET /api/search?artist_name=<a>&track_name=<t>`; if that returns nothing, retry with the free-text `?q=<artist> <track>`.
3. **Filter + rank** the array:
   - drop `instrumental == true`
   - drop entries with no `syncedLyrics` unless `--allow-unsynced`
   - drop `abs(duration - video_duration) > --duration-tolerance` (default **5.0 s**; a tighter default is right because a wrong match is worse than no match, and the flag is right there)
   - score = `0.6 * (1 - Δdur/tolerance) + 0.4 * difflib.SequenceMatcher(None, norm(artist_api), norm(artist_ours)).ratio()`, where `norm` casefolds, strips punctuation/whitespace, and NFKC-normalises
   - sort desc
4. **Disambiguation**: auto-pick the top candidate and print the decision to stderr —
   `[ytmv] lrclib: "<trackName>" — <artistName> (Δ2.0s, score 0.91; 3 candidates, --pick to choose)`.
   With `--pick` (or `pick_on_ambiguous = true` in config) **and** a TTY **and** more than one candidate within 0.1 score of the top, show a `rich` table and prompt. Non-TTY always auto-picks — batch runs must never block.
5. **YouTube captions fallback.** Fetch VTT via yt-dlp (`writesubtitles: True`, `writeautomaticsub: <--allow-auto-captions>`, `subtitlesformat: "vtt"`, `skip_download: True`) and convert with our own **`vtt_to_lrc()`**.
   **Do not use `yt-dlp --convert-subs lrc`** even though it exists: it does not deduplicate YouTube's rolling auto-caption repetition (each cue repeats the previous visible line — the exact problem `scripts/yth/__init__.py::vtt_to_text` solves for the untimed case), so auto-captions come out as unreadable LRC. Our timed variant reuses that dedupe logic plus `<…>` inline-tag stripping and requires no ffmpeg. ~30 lines, offline-testable, worth owning.
   **Auto-captions are off by default** (`--allow-auto-captions` to enable): for music, ASR lyrics are usually wrong, and wrong lyrics burned into a video are worse than none. When used, the LRC gets `[by:YouTube auto-captions]` and a stderr warning.
6. **`plainLyrics` (unsynced).** Enough for USLT, which is how most players display a static lyric page. Writes USLT only — no `.lrc`, no SRT. Report record carries `"synced": false`.
7. **Give up.** stderr note, continue with the media, exit 0. With `--require-lyrics`: skip that track entirely and set the final exit to 1.

### Cache

`cache_dir()/lrclib/<sha256(normalised query)>.json`, storing `{"fetched_at": iso, "endpoint": …, "query": {…}, "result": {…}|null}`.

- Hits: **30-day** TTL. Misses: **3-day** TTL (LRCLIB gains contributions, so a miss should expire faster than a hit).
- **Negative caching matters**: re-running a 40-track playlist must not re-hammer 40 misses.
- `--refresh-lyrics` bypasses reads (still writes). `ytmv doctor` reports cache size + entry count.

### Politeness / offline

0.5 s between LRCLIB calls in a batch (`--lrclib-sleep`), single-threaded, one retry on 5xx with a 2 s backoff, no retry on 404. Complete network failure degrades to "no lyrics found" — the media still downloads (assuming YouTube is reachable), and `tag`/`profiles` remain fully functional offline.

---

## G. Playlist / batch handling

- **Inputs**: positional accepts video URLs, playlist URLs, and bare 11-char ids. Reuse `scripts.yth.extract_video_id` (`scripts/yth/__init__.py`) — it already handles `youtu.be`, `/shorts/`, `/embed/`, `/live/`, `music.youtube.com`, and bare ids, and is anchored against query-string spoofing. See §I for the import-safety argument.
- **`--from-file`**: one URL per line, `#` comments, blanks skipped.
- **Playlists**: `extract_flat: "in_playlist"` first to enumerate cheaply, then a full `extract_info` per entry. `--playlist-items` passes through; `--max N` stops early.
- **`--number`**: zero-padded prefix from the playlist index, width `max(profile.number_width, len(str(total)))` → `01 - Artist - Track.mp3`. **On by default for playlists, off for single URLs** — this is precisely the "old player sorts by FAT directory order / filename" problem, and playlists are the only place ordering is meaningful.
- **`--m3u`**: on by default for playlists. Writes `<outdir>/<Playlist Title>.m3u` (not `.m3u8`) with CRLF, **relative** paths, `#EXTM3U` + `#EXTINF:<secs>,<Artist> - <Track>`, encoded with the profile's `lrc_encoding` — a UTF-8 m3u produces mojibake on a cp950 player exactly like a UTF-8 `.lrc` does.
- **Concurrency: sequential, `--sleep 1.5`** (mirrors `scripts/yth/fetch_subs.py` `sleep: float = 1.5`). No `--jobs`, deliberately: YouTube bot-checks this host aggressively (a confirmed environment fact), and the ffmpeg transcode is CPU-bound so parallel downloads buy little. Document the omission so it doesn't read as an oversight.
- **Resume / skip**: file-existence based, no database. Before download, if the full artifact set for the computed basename exists and `--force` is absent → `[ytmv] skip: <name> (exists)`. `continuedl: True` lets yt-dlp resume `.part` files. Everything is produced in a `TemporaryDirectory` and `os.replace`d in, so a partial artifact never satisfies the skip check.
- **`--manifest <path>`**: optional JSONL append, one record per produced artifact (`{ts, url, video_id, artist, track, profile, artifact, path, lyrics_source, synced}`). Feeds ad-hoc `jq` reporting without introducing a schema to migrate.
- **Failure isolation**: a per-URL `try/except` like `scripts/yth/fetch_subs.py:120-126` — one bad video never aborts the batch; a summary line goes to stderr at the end; exit 1 if any track failed, 0 otherwise.

---

## H. Output layout

**Default output dir**: `platformdirs.user_music_dir() / "ytmv"` → `~/Music/ytmv` on both macOS and Linux (and it honours `XDG_MUSIC_DIR` from `~/.config/user-dirs.dirs` on Linux). Not XDG data — this is user media, not application state. Resolution: `--out` > `$YTMV_OUT` (the test override, mirroring `$YTH_DB`'s "(tests)" role at `scripts/yth/__init__.py::db_path`) > `output_dir` in config.toml > `~/Music/ytmv`.

**Structure — `flat` by default**:

| layout | path |
|---|---|
| `flat` *(default)* | `<out>/Artist - Track.mp3` |
| `artist` | `<out>/Artist/Track.mp3` |
| `artist-album` | `<out>/Artist/Album/NN Track.mp3` |
| `playlist` *(default when a playlist URL is given)* | `<out>/Playlist Title/NN - Artist - Track.mp3` |

Flat is the default because old players index a folder and their on-device navigation makes deep trees painful; `artist-album` exists for the iPod-class devices that build a real library.

**FAT32 mapping** (`scripts/ytmv/naming.py`, `filename_style = "fat32"`):
- Strip `" * / : < > ? \ |` and all control chars; replace with nothing (not `_`) except where that would collide two adjacent words, then collapse runs of whitespace.
- Strip trailing dots and spaces (FAT32 cannot store them; Windows/macOS silently rewrite them).
- Reject reserved DOS basenames `CON PRN AUX NUL COM1-9 LPT1-9` (case-insensitive, with or without extension) → suffix `_`.
- Cap each path component at `filename_max_len` (default 64), truncating on a word boundary where possible, always preserving the extension.
- **Hard invariant, tested**: the sidecar `.lrc` / `.srt` / `.txt` basename is byte-identical to the media basename. That equality is the *only* way any player finds the sidecar, and it is the easiest thing to break with a truncation off-by-one. `naming.py` returns a single `stem` and every artifact derives from it — the code cannot express a mismatch.

**`filename_style = "ascii"`** is honest about its limits: NFKD gives Chinese no ASCII form, so non-ASCII maps to `_`, runs collapse, and if the result is empty or all-underscores the stem becomes `track-<videoid>`. A stderr warning fires. Documented as "for players that show `????` in filenames — the ID3 tags and `.lrc` still carry the real text."

**USB / SD workflow**: `ytmv get URL --out /Volumes/MP3 --profile safe` writes straight to the card. Proposed nicety (see §K): detect a FAT/exFAT mount (`os.statvfs` + `diskutil info -plist` on macOS / `findmnt -no FSTYPE` on Linux) and, if the user hasn't chosen a profile, auto-select `safe` with a note.

## I. File-by-file implementation plan

### Module split

```
dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_ytmv        launcher: USAGE short-circuit, _source_path(),
                                        dict dispatch to leaves. ~200 lines.
scripts/ytmv/__init__.py                APP="ytmv", dirs, load_config, exit codes,
                                        note()/warn(), ffmpeg discovery + cached caps
                                        probe, cookie resolution, ytdl() lazy import,
                                        url/id helpers. ~350 lines.
scripts/ytmv/profile.py                 Profile dataclass, PROFILES dict,
                                        resolve_profile(). Pure. ~200 lines.
scripts/ytmv/naming.py                  sanitise(), build_stem(), build_paths().
                                        Pure. ~150 lines.
scripts/ytmv/lrc.py                     parse_lrc, render_lrc, vtt_to_lrc, lrc_to_srt,
                                        write_encoded(). Pure. ~250 lines.
scripts/ytmv/lrclib.py                  urllib client, cache, rank, pick. ~220 lines.
scripts/ytmv/meta.py                    derive() metadata chain + title parsing.
                                        Pure given an info dict. ~150 lines.
scripts/ytmv/tagging.py                 mutagen ID3 writer (v2.3/v2.4, USLT, SYLT,
                                        APIC), read_tags(). ~250 lines.
scripts/ytmv/media.py                   yt-dlp opts builders, download_one(), ffmpeg
                                        wrappers: transcode, cover, mux, burn. ~350 lines.
scripts/ytmv/get.py                     leaf
scripts/ytmv/lyrics.py                  leaf
scripts/ytmv/tag.py                     leaf
scripts/ytmv/search.py                  leaf
scripts/ytmv/profiles.py                leaf (note: support module is profile.py, singular)
scripts/ytmv/doctor.py                  leaf
```

`__init__.py` must **not** import any of the support modules at module level (`scripts/yth/__init__.py` imports only stdlib at top level; keep that property so `--help` and `profiles` stay instant).

PEP-723 block: `requires-python = ">=3.11"`, deps `yt-dlp>=2025.1`, `tyro>=0.9`, `rich>=13.9`, `platformdirs>=4`, `mutagen>=1.47`. No `httpx` (§F).

### Cookie sharing — the recommended answer

**Import yth's helpers, with yth's config as a fallback source, not a duplicate.**

```python
def cookie_opts_for(cfg: dict) -> dict:
    # 1. ytmv's own config wins.
    if cfg.get("cookiefile") or cfg.get("from_browser"):
        return _own_cookie_opts(cfg)
    # 2. Fall back to yth's — one cookie jar per machine is the right model,
    #    and the user has probably already configured it there.
    try:
        from scripts.yth import cookie_opts, load_config as yth_config
        return cookie_opts(yth_config())
    except Exception:          # yth absent / broken → no cookies, which is
        return {}              # correct for public videos anyway.
```

Safe because `scripts/yth/__init__.py` imports only stdlib at module level, `cookie_opts` returns yt-dlp kwargs in exactly the shape we need, and the fallback is wrapped so a broken `yth` can never break `ytmv`. It also inherits yth's Zen-profile autodetection for free. The coupling goes in **both** tools' "Cross-file invariants" sections (`docs/tools/yth.md:115-129` gains a bullet).

### Suggested build order

1. `profile.py` + `naming.py` + `lrc.py` (pure, no I/O) → the `profiles` leaf → first bats tests. **Ship this and verify offline before any network code.**
2. `tagging.py` + the `tag` leaf → round-trip test on a fixture MP3.
3. `lrclib.py` + the `search` leaf.
4. `__init__.py` ffmpeg discovery + `doctor`.
5. `meta.py` + `media.py` + `get` (audio path only, `--mode audio`).
6. `get` video path: softsub, then hardsub.
7. `lyrics` leaf (mostly composition of 2+3).
8. Completions, docs, registration.

## J. Verification plan

### Offline, no network, no ffmpeg

These are the bulk of the tests and cover the bulk of the risk:

| Target | Test |
|---|---|
| Profile resolution | `ytmv profiles --json` — every built-in resolves; `inherits` chains work; a config-file `[profiles.x]` overriding a built-in wins; a cycle errors with exit 2 not a stack overflow; a CLI flag beats `[defaults]` beats profile beats `safe`. |
| LRC parse | 3-digit vs 2-digit vs no fractional; repeated timestamps on one line; `[offset:]` sign; metadata tags excluded from cues; unsorted input sorted; blank cues dropped. |
| LRC → SRT | end = next start; `max_dur` clamp; last-line clamp to track duration; equal-timestamp guard; `HH:MM:SS,mmm` format. |
| VTT → LRC | rolling auto-caption dedupe; `<c>` / `<00:00:01.234>` tag stripping; header lines dropped. |
| Encoding transcode | UTF-8 → cp950 round-trip; an unencodable char under `warn-replace` produces `?` **and** a stderr warning with a count; under `fail` exits 1; under `utf8` silently keeps UTF-8 and says so. CRLF vs LF byte-exact. |
| Filename sanitisation | FAT32-illegal chars; trailing dot/space; `CON.mp3`; length cap preserving extension; **`.lrc` stem == media stem** for every style and every cap; `ascii` on a pure-CJK title yields `track-<id>`, not empty. |
| ID3 round-trip | Write with `--profile safe`, read back with mutagen: `ID3v2.3`, UTF-16 `TIT2`/`TPE1`, `USLT` present with the right lang/desc, no `SYLT`, APIC ≤ 300 px, ID3v1 tail present. Then `--profile modern` on the same file: v2.4, UTF-8, `SYLT` present. Then back to `safe` — no v4-only frame survives. |
| Metadata derivation | A table of ~15 real title shapes (`Artist - Title (Official MV)`, `【MV】Artist - Title`, `Title | Channel`, no-separator + `Artist - Topic` uploader) → expected `(artist, track, confidence)`. |
| Launcher | `--help` exits 0 and prints `USAGE` **without importing yt_dlp or mutagen** (run it with bare `python3`, the way `tests/unit/herdr_grep.bats:613` does — this only works if the help short-circuit stays strictly stdlib). Unknown subcommand → 2. |
| Completion sync | Mirror `tests/unit/herdr_grep.bats:610-624` exactly: assert every public flag appears in `--help` **and** both completion files, plus every profile name and every `--mode`/`--lyrics-out` value. |

The MP3 fixture: base64 a ~400-byte silent single-frame MP3 inline in the `.bats` file and decode it in `setup()`. Self-contained, reviewable in a diff, no binary blob in the repo, no ffmpeg dependency.

`tests/unit/ytmv.bats` uses `command -v uv >/dev/null || skip` for the tests that need real deps (uv's PEP-723 resolve is cached, so it's fast after the first run) and `setup_path_stub` (`tests/test_helper.bash:19`) with a fake `ffmpeg` that logs its argv for the pipeline-shape tests. Export `YTMV_OUT` and `XDG_*` into `$BATS_TMPDIR` so nothing touches `~/Music`.

Note the tension with `docs/this_repo/testing.md:19` ("Python script tests" are out of scope): this follows the `herdr_grep.bats` / `x_cli.bats` precedent of **offline black-box CLI tests**, not unit tests of Python internals. Worth a one-line acknowledgement in the PR (§K).

### Needs network

- `ytmv search "<artist> <track>" --json` — LRCLIB reachable, ranking sane. No YouTube, no cookies, no browser login. **This is the best early smoke test.**
- `ytmv get <public-url> --dry-run --json` — full metadata + lyric resolution + output paths, zero bytes of media downloaded. Exercises the whole decision path.
- `ytmv get <public-url> --mode audio` — real end-to-end. Cookie-free for public videos; if the bot-check fires, `--cookies` picks up yth's configured source.

## K. Risks and open questions — please decide before implementation

1. **`ffmpeg@7` in `media_tools`?** Without a libass build, the *default* profile's hardsub output is impossible and `--everything` is permanently one-quarter degraded. Adding it inside the already-gated role is allowed by `CLAUDE.md:26`; it costs a large keg-only bottle on macOS. **Alternatives**: leave it out and require manual `brew install ffmpeg@7` with a doctor hint, or use `ffmpeg-full`. My recommendation: **add `ffmpeg@7`** — keg-only means zero shadowing risk, and the CLI's flagship feature depends on it. Your call.
2. **`cp950`/`cp936` vs `big5`/`gbk` as the actual codecs.** I recommend the MS supersets under the friendlier profile names, because Python's strict `big5` raises on characters real players display fine. Confirm.
3. **SYLT default.** Off everywhere except `modern`, in my design. If you have any reason to think your player reads SYLT, say so and I'll flip `safe`. (There is a real, if small, risk that a malformed SYLT makes a fragile parser reject the whole tag.)
4. **Cookie coupling to `yth`.** I recommend reading `~/.config/yth/config.toml` as the fallback cookie source via `from scripts.yth import cookie_opts`. Confirm you want one cookie jar per machine rather than two independent configs.
5. **Output root.** `~/Music/ytmv` (via `platformdirs.user_music_dir()`) vs cwd vs an XDG data dir. I recommend `~/Music/ytmv`. Also: should a FAT/exFAT `--out` auto-select the `safe` profile with a note? I think yes.
6. **`--mode`/`--lyrics-out` vs four named modes.** I split *media* from *lyric delivery* rather than shipping four opaque mode names, because (a) and (b) are the same MP3 with different attachments. `--everything` still gives you all four in one command. Confirm you're happy with the decomposition.
7. **Name.** `ytmv` — confirm.
8. **Auto-captions default-off.** I default `--allow-auto-captions` to false because ASR lyrics for music are usually wrong, and wrong lyrics burned into a video are worse than none. Confirm.
9. **`.txt` plain-lyrics sidecar** — I enabled it only in the CJK profiles (some Chinese-market firmware reads `.txt`). Do you want it in `safe` too?
10. **Test scope.** `docs/this_repo/testing.md:19` lists Python script tests as out of scope; `tests/unit/ytmv.bats` follows the `herdr_grep`/`x_cli` precedent (offline black-box CLI tests, not internals). Confirm you want the bats file, and whether the base64-inline MP3 fixture is acceptable.
11. **Content/ToS.** Docs should stay neutral: this is a personal-archival tool, lyrics come from LRCLIB (a community database) and are attached to your own local files. Worth one sentence in `docs/tools/ytmv.md` so the intent is on the record.
12. **`docs/shells/aliases.zh-TW.md` is stale** (missing `yth` and `appsrc` rows already). Skip it for `ytmv` too and keep the drift consistent, or fix it as a separate change? I recommend skipping now, filing a `TODO.md` item.

```python
yt-dlp's job here is narrow: fetch the media, convert the container/codec, and

``--embed-metadata`` / ``--embed-thumbnail`` postprocessors are deliberately NOT
used: they only write ID3v2.4 and would fight with mutagen over the same frames.

Output modes (combinable):

  --video                      mp4 (h264/aac), soft subs by default

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# URL collection
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
def _normalize(url: str) -> str:
    """Accept a bare 11-char video id as well as a full URL."""
    url = url.strip()
    if len(url) == 11 and "/" not in url and ":" not in url:
        return f"https://www.youtube.com/watch?v={url}"
    return url


def collect_urls(args: Args) -> list[str]:
    urls = [_normalize(u) for u in args.urls if u.strip()]
    if args.from_file:
        path = Path(args.from_file).expanduser()
        if not path.is_file():
            print(f"ytmv get: no such file: {path}", file=sys.stderr)
            return []
        for line in path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines():
            line = line.strip()
            if line and not line.startswith("#"):
                urls.append(_normalize(line))
    return urls


def expand_playlists(urls: list[str], cookies: dict) -> list[str]:
    """Flatten playlist URLs into their entries; leave single videos alone."""
    yt_dlp = ytdl()
    out: list[str] = []
    for url in urls:
        if "list=" not in url:
            out.append(url)
            continue
        opts = {"extract_flat": "in_playlist", "skip_download": True,
                "quiet": True, "no_warnings": True, **cookies}
        try:
            with yt_dlp.YoutubeDL(opts) as ydl:
                info = ydl.extract_info(url, download=False)
        except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001
            print(f"ytmv get: cannot expand playlist {url}: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
            continue
        for entry in (info or {}).get("entries") or []:
            if entry and entry.get("id"):
                out.append(f"https://www.youtube.com/watch?v={entry['id']}")
    return out


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# yt-dlp calls
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
def _base_opts(ffmpeg: str | None, cookies: dict) -> dict:
    opts = {"quiet": True, "no_warnings": True, "noprogress": True, **cookies}
    if ffmpeg:
        opts["ffmpeg_location"] = ffmpeg
    return opts


def probe(url: str, ffmpeg: str | None, cookies: dict) -> dict | None:
    yt_dlp = ytdl()
    opts = {**_base_opts(ffmpeg, cookies), "skip_download": True}
    try:
        with yt_dlp.YoutubeDL(opts) as ydl:
            return ydl.extract_info(url, download=False)
    except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001
        print(f"  x metadata: {str(e).splitlines()[0][:160]}", file=sys.stderr)
        return None


def download_audio(url: str, workdir: Path, quality: str, ffmpeg: str | None,
                   cookies: dict) -> Path | None:
    yt_dlp = ytdl()
    opts = {
        **_base_opts(ffmpeg, cookies),
        "format": "bestaudio/best",
        "outtmpl": {"default": str(workdir / "audio.%(ext)s")},
        "writethumbnail": True,
        "postprocessors": [
            {"key": "FFmpegExtractAudio", "preferredcodec": "mp3",
             "preferredquality": quality},
        ],
    }
    with yt_dlp.YoutubeDL(opts) as ydl:
        ydl.download([url])
    hits = sorted(workdir.glob("audio.mp3"))
    return hits[0] if hits else None


def download_video(url: str, workdir: Path, max_height: int, soft_subs: bool,
                   langs: list[str], ffmpeg: str | None, cookies: dict) -> Path | None:
    yt_dlp = ytdl()
    height = f"[height<={max_height}]" if max_height else ""
    postprocessors: list[dict] = []
    if soft_subs:
        postprocessors.append({"key": "FFmpegEmbedSubtitle"})
    opts = {
        **_base_opts(ffmpeg, cookies),
        # h264 + aac: the only combination old hardware decoders reliably handle.
        "format": f"bv*{height}+ba/b{height}",
        "format_sort": ["vcodec:h264", "acodec:aac", "res", "fps"],
        "merge_output_format": "mp4",
        "outtmpl": {"default": str(workdir / "video.%(ext)s")},
        "writesubtitles": soft_subs,
        "writeautomaticsub": soft_subs,
        "subtitleslangs": langs or ["en"],
        "postprocessors": postprocessors,
    }
    with yt_dlp.YoutubeDL(opts) as ydl:
        ydl.download([url])
    for candidate in ("video.mp4", "video.mkv", "video.webm"):
        path = workdir / candidate
        if path.is_file():
            return path
    return None


def youtube_lrc(url: str, workdir: Path, langs: list[str], ffmpeg: str | None,
                cookies: dict) -> str:
    """Fetch YouTube captions already converted to LRC by yt-dlp itself."""
    yt_dlp = ytdl()
    subdir = workdir / "subs"
    subdir.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    opts = {
        **_base_opts(ffmpeg, cookies),
        "skip_download": True,
        "writesubtitles": True,
        "writeautomaticsub": True,
        "subtitleslangs": langs or ["en"],
        "subtitlesformat": "vtt",
        "outtmpl": {"default": str(subdir / "%(id)s.%(ext)s")},
        "postprocessors": [{"key": "FFmpegSubtitlesConvertor", "format": "lrc",
                            "when": "before_dl"}],
        "sleep_interval_subtitles": 1,
    }
    try:
        with yt_dlp.YoutubeDL(opts) as ydl:
            ydl.download([url])
    except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001
        print(f"  - captions: {str(e).splitlines()[0][:120]}", file=sys.stderr)
        return ""
    for path in sorted(subdir.glob("*.lrc")):
        text = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
        if text.strip():
            return text
    return ""


def burn_subs(ffmpeg: str, video: Path, lrc_text: str, dest: Path,
              workdir: Path) -> tuple[bool, str]:
    """Burn LRC lyrics into the picture via an intermediate SRT."""
    srt_text = lrc_to_srt(lrc_text)
    if not srt_text:
        return False, "no timed lyrics to burn"
    srt = workdir / "burn.srt"
    srt.write_text(srt_text, encoding="utf-8")
    # The filter argument is a path; ':' and '\' are filter-syntax metacharacters,
    # so keep it inside the temp dir and escape defensively.
    escaped = str(srt).replace("\\", "\\\\").replace(":", r"\:").replace("'", r"\'")
    code, err = run_ffmpeg(
        ffmpeg,
        [
            "-i", str(video),
            "-vf", f"subtitles='{escaped}':force_style='FontSize=22,Outline=1,MarginV=24'",
            "-c:v", "libx264", "-preset", "medium", "-crf", "23",
            "-c:a", "aac", "-b:a", "192k",
            str(dest),
        ],
    )
    return code == 0, err


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# Main flow
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
def build_stem(meta: dict, settings: dict, index: int | None) -> str:
    parts = [p for p in (meta.get("artist"), meta.get("track")) if p]
    raw = " - ".join(parts) if len(parts) == 2 else (parts[0] if parts else "untitled")
    if index is not None:
        raw = f"{index:02d} - {raw}"
    return sanitize_filename(raw, settings["filename_charset"], settings["filename_max"])


def process_one(url: str, index: int | None, args: Args, cfg: dict, settings: dict,
                out_dir: Path, ffmpeg: str | None, cookies: dict, langs: list[str]) -> dict:
    result: dict = {"url": url, "status": "error", "files": []}

    info = probe(url, ffmpeg, cookies)
    if not info:
        result["detail"] = "metadata lookup failed"
        return result

    meta = parse_artist_track(info, args.artist, args.track, args.album)
    result["metadata"] = meta
    duration = info.get("duration")
    stem = build_stem(meta, settings, index if args.number else None)
    result["stem"] = stem

    mp3_dest = out_dir / f"{stem}.mp3"
    mp4_dest = out_dir / f"{stem}.mp4"
    want_audio = args.audio
    want_video = args.video or args.burn_subs
    if not args.force:
        if want_audio and mp3_dest.is_file() and mp3_dest.stat().st_size:
            want_audio = False
        if want_video and mp4_dest.is_file() and mp4_dest.stat().st_size:
            want_video = False
    if not want_audio and not want_video:
        result["status"] = "skipped"
        result["files"] = [str(p) for p in (mp3_dest, mp4_dest) if p.is_file()]
        return result

    # ---- lyrics (needed by both the mp3 tags and the hardsub) ----
    synced = plain = ""
    lyrics_source = "disabled"
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="ytmv-") as td:
        workdir = Path(td)

        if args.lyrics in ("auto", "lrclib"):
            synced, plain, lyrics_source = fetch_lyrics(
                meta["artist"], meta["track"], duration, meta["album"],
                interactive=False, use_cache=not args.no_cache,
            )
        if not synced and args.lyrics in ("auto", "youtube"):
            captions = youtube_lrc(url, workdir, langs, ffmpeg, cookies)
            if captions.strip():
                synced = captions
                plain = lrc_to_plain(captions)
                lyrics_source = "youtube-captions"
        result["lyrics_source"] = lyrics_source
        result["lyrics"] = "synced" if synced else ("unsynced" if plain else "none")

        # ---- audio ----
        if want_audio:
            try:
                produced = download_audio(url, workdir, args.audio_quality, ffmpeg, cookies)
            except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001
                result["detail"] = f"audio download failed: {str(e).splitlines()[0][:160]}"
                return result
            if not produced:
                result["detail"] = "audio download produced no mp3"
                return result

            cover = None
            if settings.get("cover") != "none" and ffmpeg:
                thumbs = [p for p in workdir.iterdir()
                          if p.suffix.lower() in (".webp", ".jpg", ".jpeg", ".png")]
                if thumbs:
                    jpeg = workdir / "cover.jpg"
                    if make_cover(ffmpeg, thumbs[0], jpeg, settings["cover_max"]):
                        cover = jpeg.read_bytes()

            tag_meta = dict(meta)
            if index is not None and args.number:
                tag_meta["track_number"] = index
            try:
                tag_mp3(produced, tag_meta, settings, lyrics_text=plain,
                        synced_lrc=synced, cover=cover)
            except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001
                result["detail"] = f"tagging failed: {type(e).__name__}: {e}"
                return result

            out_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            shutil.move(str(produced), str(mp3_dest))
            result["files"].append(str(mp3_dest))

            if synced and settings.get("lrc_sidecar"):
                try:
                    write_lrc(mp3_dest.with_suffix(".lrc"), synced,
                              settings["lrc_encoding"], settings["lrc_on_unencodable"])
                    result["files"].append(str(mp3_dest.with_suffix(".lrc")))
                except UnencodableLyrics as e:
                    # The mp3 is already good; only the sidecar failed. Say so
                    # precisely instead of failing the whole item.
                    print(f"  - sidecar .lrc: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
                    result["lrc_warning"] = str(e)

        # ---- video ----
        if want_video:
            try:
                produced = download_video(url, workdir, args.max_height,
                                          args.soft_subs and not args.burn_subs,
                                          langs, ffmpeg, cookies)
            except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001
                result["detail"] = f"video download failed: {str(e).splitlines()[0][:160]}"
                return result
            if not produced:
                result["detail"] = "video download produced no file"
                return result

            out_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            if args.burn_subs:
                ok, err = burn_subs(ffmpeg, produced, synced, mp4_dest, workdir)
                if not ok:
                    result["detail"] = f"burn-in failed: {err}"
                    return result
            else:
                shutil.move(str(produced), str(mp4_dest))
            result["files"].append(str(mp4_dest))

    result["status"] = "ok"
    return result


def cli(args: Args) -> int:
    urls = collect_urls(args)
    if not urls:
        print("ytmv get: no URLs. Try: ytmv get 'https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=...'",
              file=sys.stderr)
        return 2

    if args.lyrics not in ("auto", "lrclib", "youtube", "none"):
        print(f"ytmv get: --lyrics must be auto|lrclib|youtube|none, got "
              f"'{args.lyrics}'", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2

    cfg = load_config()
    try:
        settings = resolve_profile(cfg, args.profile, overrides_from(args))
    except KeyError as e:
        print(f"ytmv get: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2

    ffmpeg = ffmpeg_bin(cfg)
    if not ffmpeg:
        print("ytmv get: ffmpeg not found — it is required to produce mp3/mp4.\n"
              "  Re-run chezmoi init with installMediaTools=true, or set\n"
              "  ffmpeg = \"/path/to/ffmpeg\" in ~/.config/ytmv/config.toml.",
              file=sys.stderr)
        return 3

    if args.burn_subs and not has_libass(ffmpeg):
        # Falling back to soft subs here would hand back a file the player shows
        # nothing on — the exact failure this tool exists to prevent.
        print(libass_help(ffmpeg), file=sys.stderr)
        return 3

    out_dir = Path(args.out).expanduser() if args.out else (
        Path(str(cfg["out"])).expanduser() if cfg.get("out") else default_out_dir()
    )
    cookies = cookie_options(cfg, args.cookies)
    langs = args.langs or cfg.get("langs") or []
    if not langs:
        try:
            from scripts.yth import load_config as yth_config

            langs = yth_config().get("langs") or ["en"]
        except ImportError:
            langs = ["en"]

    urls = expand_playlists(urls, cookies)
    if (args.artist or args.track or args.album) and len(urls) > 1:
        print(f"ytmv get: --artist/--track/--album apply to a single video; got "
              f"{len(urls)}.", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2

    results = []
    ok = failed = skipped = 0
    total = len(urls)
    for i, url in enumerate(urls, 1):
        print(f"[{i}/{total}] {url}", file=sys.stderr)
        result = process_one(url, i, args, cfg, settings, out_dir, ffmpeg, cookies, langs)
        results.append(result)
        if result["status"] == "ok":
            ok += 1
            print(f"  ok {result.get('stem')}  "
                  f"[lyrics: {result.get('lyrics')} via {result.get('lyrics_source')}]"
                  f"  [meta: {result.get('metadata', {}).get('source')}]", file=sys.stderr)
        elif result["status"] == "skipped":
            skipped += 1
            print("  - already present (--force to redo)", file=sys.stderr)
        else:
            failed += 1
            print(f"  x {result.get('detail')}", file=sys.stderr)
        if args.sleep and i < total:
            time.sleep(args.sleep)

    if args.m3u:
        _write_m3u(out_dir, args.m3u, results)

    if args.json_out:
        import json

        print(json.dumps(results, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False))

    print(f"ytmv get: {ok} downloaded, {skipped} skipped, {failed} failed → {out_dir}",
          file=sys.stderr)
    return 1 if failed else 0


def _write_m3u(out_dir: Path, name: str, results: list[dict]) -> None:
    """Emit a plain .m3u of the audio files, in the order they were requested."""
    lines = ["#EXTM3U"]
    for result in results:
        for path in result.get("files", []):
            if path.endswith(".mp3"):
                lines.append(Path(path).name)
    target = out_dir / (name if name.endswith(".m3u") else f"{name}.m3u")
    try:
        out_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        target.write_text("\n".join(lines) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
        print(f"[ytmv] playlist: {target}", file=sys.stderr)
    except OSError as e:
        print(f"ytmv get: could not write {target}: {e}", file=sys.stderr)


def main() -> int:
    return cli(tyro.cli(Args, prog="ytmv get"))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

```

```
#!/usr/bin/env -S uv run --quiet --script
# /// script
# requires-python = ">=3.11"
# dependencies = [
#   "yt-dlp>=2025.1",
#   "tyro>=0.9",
#   "rich>=13.9",
#   "platformdirs>=4",
#   "mutagen>=1.47",
#   "httpx>=0.27",
# ]
# ///
"""ytmv — download YouTube music videos for playback on old MP3 players.

yt-dlp gets you a file; it does not get you a file a 2008 player can use. This
adds the compatibility layer on top: ID3v2.3 instead of v2.4, optional raw
Big5/GBK text frames, a sidecar .lrc in the encoding the device expects,
FAT32-safe filenames, small JPEG cover art, and real synced lyrics from LRCLIB
(official music videos usually carry no YouTube captions at all).

Subcommands:
  get <URL>…                     Download → convert → tag → attach lyrics.
      [--audio] [--video]        mp3 (default) and/or mp4.
      [--burn-subs]              Burn lyrics into the picture (needs libass).
      [--profile NAME]           Player compatibility profile.
  lyrics <PATH>…                 Find + attach lyrics to existing mp3s.
      [--pick] [--artist/--track]  Resolve ambiguous LRCLIB matches by hand.
  tag <PATH>…                    Re-apply a profile to existing files. Offline —
                                 this is the "try another profile" loop.
  doctor [--list-profiles]       Probe yt-dlp / ffmpeg / libass / cookies and
                                 print the fully resolved profile.

Profiles (--profile): safe (default) · cjk-big5 · cjk-gbk · ipod · modern.
When the player is unknown, start with `safe`, copy one file across, and use
`ytmv tag` to bisect from there — no re-downloading required.

Config at user_config_dir/ytmv/config.toml; cache at user_cache_dir/ytmv.
Cookies are read from `yth`'s config (docs/tools/yth.md § Cookies) so there is
only ever one cookie jar per machine.

Sibling of `yth` (dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_yth), which searches your watch
history but deliberately never downloads. Logic lives in scripts/ytmv/*.py.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

USAGE = """\
Usage: ytmv <subcommand> [args...]

  get <URL>...                       Download + convert + tag + lyrics.
      [--audio] [--video]            mp3 (default) and/or mp4.
      [--burn-subs]                  Burn lyrics into the picture (needs libass).
      [--profile NAME] [--out DIR]   Compatibility profile / output directory.
      [--number] [--m3u NAME]        Playlist ordering helpers for old players.
      [--cookies]                    Use yth's cookie source (bot checks).
  lyrics <PATH>...                   Attach lyrics to mp3s you already have.
      [--pick] [--artist A --track T]
  tag <PATH>...                      Re-apply a profile in place. No network.
      [--profile NAME] [--rename] [--dry-run]
  doctor [--list-profiles] [--json]  Environment probe + resolved profile.

Profiles: safe (default) | cjk-big5 | cjk-gbk | ipod | modern

Examples:
  ytmv get 'https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=...'
  ytmv get '<playlist-url>' --number --m3u roadtrip --out /Volumes/MP3
  ytmv get '<url>' --video --burn-subs --max-height 480
  ytmv tag ~/Music/ytmv --profile cjk-big5      # player showed mojibake
  ytmv lyrics ~/Music/ytmv/*.mp3 --pick
  ytmv doctor
"""


def _source_path() -> Path:
    """Locate the chezmoi source dir so we can import scripts.ytmv.*.

    Identical strategy to executable_yth:_source_path / executable_mlf.
    Trust `chezmoi source-path`; fall back to ~/.local/share/chezmoi.
    """
    chezmoi = shutil.which("chezmoi")
    if chezmoi:
        try:
            out = subprocess.run(
                [chezmoi, "source-path"],
                capture_output=True, text=True, check=False, timeout=5,
            )
            if out.returncode == 0 and out.stdout.strip():
                return Path(out.stdout.strip())
        except (subprocess.TimeoutExpired, OSError):
            pass
    fallback = Path.home() / ".local" / "share" / "chezmoi"
    if (fallback / "scripts" / "ytmv" / "__init__.py").is_file():
        return fallback
    print(
        "ytmv: cannot locate chezmoi source dir.\n"
        "  Tried: `chezmoi source-path` and ~/.local/share/chezmoi.\n"
        "  Install chezmoi or ensure the source dir exists.",
        file=sys.stderr,
    )
    sys.exit(2)


def _leaf(module: str, prog: str, args: list[str]) -> int:
    """Rewrite argv and hand off to a leaf module's tyro-based main()."""
    sys.argv = [prog, *args]
    mod = __import__(f"scripts.ytmv.{module}", fromlist=["main"])
    return mod.main()


def main() -> int:
    # Help paths print USAGE and exit BEFORE any heavy import, so `ytmv -h`
    # stays instant and never loads yt_dlp / mutagen.
    if len(sys.argv) < 2 or sys.argv[1] in ("-h", "--help", "help"):
        # Bare `ytmv` is usage, not a picker: unlike `yth` there is no local
        # index to fuzzy-pick over, so there is no `tv ytmv` channel to exec.
        print(USAGE)
        return 0 if len(sys.argv) >= 2 else 2

    src = _source_path()
    if str(src) not in sys.path:
        sys.path.insert(0, str(src))

    sub = sys.argv[1]
    rest = sys.argv[2:]

    # Leaf modules own their own tyro parsing. Subcommand `-` → module `_`.
    leaves = {
        "get": ("get", "ytmv get"),
        "lyrics": ("lyrics", "ytmv lyrics"),
        "tag": ("tag", "ytmv tag"),
        "doctor": ("doctor", "ytmv doctor"),
    }
    if sub in leaves:
        module, prog = leaves[sub]
        return _leaf(module, prog, rest)

    print(f"ytmv: unknown subcommand '{sub}'\n\n{USAGE}", file=sys.stderr)
    return 2


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

```

```python
#!/usr/bin/env -S uv run --quiet --script
# /// script
# requires-python = ">=3.11"
# dependencies = ["mutagen>=1.47", "platformdirs>=4"]
# ///
"""Offline verification of ytmv's pure functions + the ID3 round-trip."""
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path

SRC = subprocess.run(["chezmoi", "source-path"], capture_output=True, text=True).stdout.strip()
sys.path.insert(0, SRC)

from scripts.ytmv import (  # noqa: E402
    PROFILES, UnencodableLyrics, dedupe_lrc, encode_text, lrc_to_plain, lrc_to_srt,
    parse_artist_track, parse_lrc, resolve_profile, sanitize_filename, tag_mp3,
)

fails = []


def check(name, got, want):
    if got != want:
        fails.append(f"{name}\n    got:  {got!r}\n    want: {want!r}")
        print(f"FAIL {name}")
    else:
        print(f"ok   {name}")


# ---- parse_lrc -----------------------------------------------------------
cues, meta = parse_lrc("[ar:A]\n[ti:T]\n[00:12.34]one\n[01:05]two\n[00:05.5]zero\n")
check("parse_lrc sorts by time", [c[1] for c in cues], ["zero", "one", "two"])
check("parse_lrc ms padding (.5 -> 500ms)", cues[0][0], 5500)
check("parse_lrc 2-digit frac", cues[1][0], 12340)
check("parse_lrc no frac", cues[2][0], 65000)
check("parse_lrc metadata excluded from cues", meta, {"ar": "A", "ti": "T"})

cues, _ = parse_lrc("[00:10.00][00:20.00]repeated\n")
check("parse_lrc repeated timestamps expand", [c[0] for c in cues], [10000, 20000])

cues, _ = parse_lrc("[offset:+500]\n[00:10.00]x\n")
check("parse_lrc applies [offset:]", cues[0][0], 10500)

# ---- lrc_to_srt ----------------------------------------------------------
srt = lrc_to_srt("[00:01.00]first\n[00:04.00]second\n")
check(
    "lrc_to_srt end = next start, last +5s",
    srt,
    "1\n00:00:01,000 --> 00:00:04,000\nfirst\n\n"
    "2\n00:00:04,000 --> 00:00:09,000\nsecond\n",
)
srt = lrc_to_srt("[00:01.00]orig\n[00:01.00]trans\n[00:05.00]next\n")
check("lrc_to_srt merges same-timestamp cues", srt.split("\n\n")[0].count("\n"), 3)
check("lrc_to_srt empty input", lrc_to_srt(""), "")

# ---- dedupe_lrc ----------------------------------------------------------
rolling = "[00:01.00]line one\n[00:02.00]line one\n[00:03.00]line one line two\n[00:04.00]line three\n"
out = dedupe_lrc(rolling)
check("dedupe_lrc collapses rolling captions", len(parse_lrc(out)[0]), 2)

# ---- encode_text ---------------------------------------------------------
check("encode_text utf-8 ok", encode_text("涙そうそう", "utf-8").decode("utf-8"), "涙そうそう")
try:
    encode_text("涙そうそう", "cp950")
    fails.append("encode_text strict should have raised for cp950/kana")
    print("FAIL encode_text strict raises")
except UnencodableLyrics as e:
    check("encode_text strict names the char", "涙" in str(e) and "line 1" in str(e), True)
check(
    "encode_text replace substitutes",
    encode_text("涙そうそう", "cp950", "replace").decode("cp950"),
    "?そうそう",
)
check("cp950 accepts what big5 rejects", encode_text("碁～‧", "cp950").decode("cp950"), "碁～‧")

# ---- sanitize_filename ---------------------------------------------------
check("sanitize strips FAT-illegal", sanitize_filename('a<b>c:d"e/f\\g|h?i*j'), "a_b_c_d_e_f_g_h_i_j")
check("sanitize drops trailing dot/space", sanitize_filename("name.  "), "name")
check("sanitize guards reserved names", sanitize_filename("CON"), "_CON")
check("sanitize caps length", len(sanitize_filename("x" * 400, "unicode", 120)), 120)
check("sanitize ascii transliterates", sanitize_filename("Café", "ascii"), "Cafe")
check("sanitize ascii CJK falls back", sanitize_filename("稻香", "ascii"), "untitled")
check("sanitize collapses whitespace", sanitize_filename("a   b"), "a b")

# ---- profile resolution --------------------------------------------------
p = resolve_profile({}, "")
check("default profile is safe", p["_name"], "safe")
check("safe is ID3v2.3", p["id3_version"], 3)
p = resolve_profile({}, "cjk-big5")
check("cjk-big5 uses cp950", p["lrc_encoding"], "cp950")
p = resolve_profile({"profile": "modern"}, "")
check("config selects profile", p["_name"], "modern")
p = resolve_profile({"profile": "modern"}, "ipod")
check("flag beats config", p["_name"], "ipod")
p = resolve_profile({}, "safe", {"id3_version": 4})
check("override beats profile", p["id3_version"], 4)
p = resolve_profile({"id3_version": 4}, "safe")
check("top-level config default applies", p["id3_version"], 4)
p = resolve_profile({"profiles": {"mine": {"id3_version": 4}}}, "mine")
check("user profile resolves", p["id3_version"], 4)
try:
    resolve_profile({}, "nope")
    fails.append("resolve_profile should raise KeyError on unknown name")
    print("FAIL resolve_profile unknown")
except KeyError as e:
    check("unknown profile lists known ones", "safe" in str(e), True)

# ---- metadata chain ------------------------------------------------------
m = parse_artist_track({"title": "X", "artist": "AA", "track": "TT"})
check("metadata: yt-dlp music fields win", (m["artist"], m["track"], m["source"]),
      ("AA", "TT", "yt-dlp-music-metadata"))
m = parse_artist_track({"title": "Band - Song (Official Music Video)"})
check("metadata: title split + noise strip", (m["artist"], m["track"], m["source"]),
      ("Band", "Song", "title-split"))
m = parse_artist_track({"title": "【MV】Band - Song"})
check("metadata: CJK bracket stripped", (m["artist"], m["track"]), ("Band", "Song"))
m = parse_artist_track({"title": "Just A Title", "channel": "Someone - Topic"})
check("metadata: channel fallback strips - Topic",
      (m["artist"], m["track"], m["source"]), ("Someone", "Just A Title", "channel-fallback"))
m = parse_artist_track({"title": "X"}, artist="Flag", track="Forced")
check("metadata: flags win", m["source"], "flags")
m = parse_artist_track({"title": "X", "upload_date": "20210304"})
check("metadata: year from upload_date", m["year"], "2021")

# ---- ID3 round-trip ------------------------------------------------------
ffmpeg = "/usr/local/bin/ffmpeg"
with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as td:
    mp3 = Path(td) / "t.mp3"
    rc = subprocess.run(
        [ffmpeg, "-hide_banner", "-loglevel", "error", "-y", "-f", "lavfi",
         "-i", "anullsrc=r=44100:cl=stereo", "-t", "1", "-q:a", "9", str(mp3)],
        capture_output=True,
    ).returncode
    if rc != 0 or not mp3.is_file():
        print("SKIP ID3 round-trip (could not synthesise an mp3)")
    else:
        from mutagen.id3 import ID3

        meta = {"artist": "歌手", "track": "稻香", "album": "Al", "year": "2008"}
        lyr = "a line\nanother line"

        tag_mp3(mp3, meta, resolve_profile({}, "safe"), lyrics_text=lyr,
                synced_lrc="[00:01.00]a line\n")
        tags = ID3(mp3)
        check("safe -> ID3v2.3", tags.version[:2], (2, 3))
        check("safe -> title round-trips", str(tags.getall("TIT2")[0].text[0]), "稻香")
        check("safe -> USLT present", len(tags.getall("USLT")), 1)
        check("safe -> no SYLT by default", len(tags.getall("SYLT")), 0)

        tag_mp3(mp3, meta, resolve_profile({}, "modern"), lyrics_text=lyr)
        tags = ID3(mp3)
        check("modern -> ID3v2.4", tags.version[:2], (2, 4))
        check("modern -> title round-trips", str(tags.getall("TIT2")[0].text[0]), "稻香")

        tag_mp3(mp3, meta, resolve_profile({}, "cjk-big5"), lyrics_text=lyr)
        tags = ID3(mp3)
        check("cjk-big5 -> ID3v2.3", tags.version[:2], (2, 3))
        raw = tags.getall("TIT2")[0]
        check("cjk-big5 -> frame declares latin-1", raw.encoding, 0)
        check("cjk-big5 -> bytes decode as cp950",
              str(raw.text[0]).encode("latin-1").decode("cp950"), "稻香")

        tag_mp3(mp3, meta, resolve_profile({}, "safe", {"embed_sylt": True}),
                lyrics_text=lyr, synced_lrc="[00:01.00]a line\n[00:03.00]b line\n")
        tags = ID3(mp3)
        check("embed_sylt writes a SYLT frame", len(tags.getall("SYLT")), 1)

        tag_mp3(mp3, meta, resolve_profile({}, "safe"), lyrics_text=lyr)
        tags = ID3(mp3)
        check("re-tag is idempotent (one TIT2)", len(tags.getall("TIT2")), 1)

# ---- lrc_to_plain --------------------------------------------------------
check("lrc_to_plain strips timestamps", lrc_to_plain("[00:01.00]a\n[00:02.00]b\n"), "a\nb")
check("lrc_to_plain passes through non-LRC", lrc_to_plain("just text"), "just text")

print()
if fails:
    print(f"{len(fails)} FAILURES:")
    for f in fails:
        print(" -", f)
    sys.exit(1)
print(f"all checks passed ({len(PROFILES)} built-in profiles)")

```

```zsh
# 60_ytmv_completion.zsh - tab completion for `ytmv` (YouTube MV -> old MP3 players).
# Source CLI: dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_ytmv (hand-rolled dispatcher) +
# scripts/ytmv/*.py (tyro leaf modules).
# Mirrors dot_config/bash/60_ytmv_completion.bash — keep both in sync.
#
# Profile names ARE completed (a small fixed built-in list, plus whatever the
# user defined) via `ytmv doctor --list-profiles`. URLs and video ids are NOT —
# they are opaque and there is no local index to enumerate.

(( $+commands[ytmv] )) || return 0

_ytmv_profiles() {
    local -a profiles
    profiles=( ${(f)"$(ytmv doctor --list-profiles 2>/dev/null)"} )
    (( ${#profiles} )) && _describe -t profiles 'player profile' profiles
}

_ytmv() {
    local context state state_descr line
    typeset -A opt_args

    _arguments -C \
        '1: :->subcommand' \
        '*::arg:->args'

    case "$state" in
        subcommand)
            local -a subs=(
                'get:Download + convert + tag + attach lyrics'
                'lyrics:Find and attach lyrics to mp3s you already have'
                'tag:Re-apply a player profile in place (offline)'
                'doctor:Probe yt-dlp / ffmpeg / libass / cookies + show the profile'
            )
            _describe -t subcommands 'ytmv subcommand' subs
            ;;
        args)
            case "$line[1]" in
                get)
                    _arguments \
                        '*:url:' \
                        '--from-file=[read URLs from a file, one per line]:file:_files' \
                        '--out=[output directory]:dir:_files -/' \
                        '--profile=[player compatibility profile]:profile:_ytmv_profiles' \
                        '--audio[produce an mp3 (default)]' \
                        '--video[also produce an mp4]' \
                        '--soft-subs[embed subtitles as an mp4 track]' \
                        '--burn-subs[burn lyrics into the picture (needs libass)]' \
                        '--lyrics=[lyrics source]:source:(auto lrclib youtube none)' \
                        '--langs=[caption languages to try]:langs:' \
                        '--artist=[override artist]:artist:' \
                        '--track=[override title]:track:' \
                        '--album=[override album]:album:' \
                        '--number[prefix filenames with 01 - ]' \
                        '--m3u=[write an .m3u playlist with this name]:name:' \
                        '--max-height=[cap video height, e.g. 480]:px:' \
                        '--audio-quality=[LAME VBR quality 0 (best) .. 9]:q:' \
                        '--cookies[use yth'"'"'s configured cookie source]' \
                        '--force[re-download even if the target exists]' \
                        '--sleep=[seconds between items]:secs:' \
                        '--refresh-lyrics[bypass the LRCLIB response cache]' \
                        '--json[emit a JSON report]' \
                        '--id3-version=[force ID3 major version]:v:(3 4)' \
                        '--id3-encoding=[ID3 text frame encoding]:enc:(utf16 utf8 latin1 raw-big5 raw-gbk)' \
                        '--lrc-encoding=[sidecar .lrc encoding]:enc:(utf-8 utf-8-sig cp950 gbk)' \
                        '--lrc-on-unencodable=[behaviour on unencodable chars]:mode:(strict replace)' \
                        '--skip-lrc-sidecar[do not write the sidecar .lrc]' \
                        '--skip-embed-lyrics[do not write a USLT frame]' \
                        '--embed-sylt[also write a SYLT frame]' \
                        '--cover-max=[longest cover edge in px]:px:' \
                        '--skip-cover[do not embed cover art]' \
                        '--ascii-filenames[transliterate filenames to ASCII]'
                    ;;
                lyrics)
                    _arguments \
                        '*:mp3 file:_files -g "*.mp3"' \
                        '--profile=[player compatibility profile]:profile:_ytmv_profiles' \
                        '--artist=[force the artist used for lookup]:artist:' \
                        '--track=[force the title used for lookup]:track:' \
                        '--album=[album, sharpens the exact lookup]:album:' \
                        '--pick[choose among LRCLIB candidates interactively]' \
                        '--force[refetch even when a sidecar .lrc exists]' \
                        '--refresh-lyrics[bypass the LRCLIB response cache]' \
                        '--sleep=[seconds between files]:secs:' \
                        '--json[emit a JSON report]' \
                        '--lrc-encoding=[sidecar .lrc encoding]:enc:(utf-8 utf-8-sig cp950 gbk)' \
                        '--lrc-on-unencodable=[behaviour on unencodable chars]:mode:(strict replace)' \
                        '--skip-lrc-sidecar[embed only, no sidecar file]' \
                        '--skip-embed-lyrics[sidecar only, no USLT frame]' \
                        '--embed-sylt[also write a SYLT frame]' \
                        '--id3-version=[force ID3 major version]:v:(3 4)' \
                        '--id3-encoding=[ID3 text frame encoding]:enc:(utf16 utf8 latin1 raw-big5 raw-gbk)' \
                        '--cover-max=[longest cover edge in px]:px:' \
                        '--skip-cover[do not embed cover art]' \
                        '--ascii-filenames[transliterate filenames to ASCII]'
                    ;;
                tag)
                    _arguments \
                        '*:mp3 file or dir:_files' \
                        '--profile=[player compatibility profile]:profile:_ytmv_profiles' \
                        '--artist=[override artist]:artist:' \
                        '--track=[override title]:track:' \
                        '--album=[override album]:album:' \
                        '--year=[override year]:year:' \
                        '--rename[rewrite filenames through the sanitiser]' \
                        '--dry-run[report what would change, write nothing]' \
                        '--id3-version=[force ID3 major version]:v:(3 4)' \
                        '--id3-encoding=[ID3 text frame encoding]:enc:(utf16 utf8 latin1 raw-big5 raw-gbk)' \
                        '--lrc-encoding=[sidecar .lrc encoding]:enc:(utf-8 utf-8-sig cp950 gbk)' \
                        '--lrc-on-unencodable=[behaviour on unencodable chars]:mode:(strict replace)' \
                        '--skip-lrc-sidecar[do not write the sidecar .lrc]' \
                        '--skip-embed-lyrics[do not write a USLT frame]' \
                        '--embed-sylt[also write a SYLT frame]' \
                        '--cover-max=[longest cover edge in px]:px:' \
                        '--skip-cover[strip / skip cover art]' \
                        '--ascii-filenames[transliterate filenames to ASCII]'
                    ;;
                doctor)
                    _arguments \
                        '--profile=[profile to resolve and display]:profile:_ytmv_profiles' \
                        '--list-profiles[print known profile names, one per line]' \
                        '--offline[skip the LRCLIB reachability check]' \
                        '--json[emit JSON instead of a table]'
                    ;;
            esac
            ;;
    esac
}
```

<tool-use data-tool-type="write" data-tool-name="Write"><details>
<summary>Tool use: **Write**</summary>

```bash
# 60_ytmv_completion.bash - tab completion for `ytmv` (YouTube MV -> old MP3 players).
# Source CLI: dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_ytmv.
# Mirrors dot_config/zsh/tools/60_ytmv_completion.zsh — keep both in sync.

command -v ytmv >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0

_ytmv_profile_list() {
    ytmv doctor --list-profiles 2>/dev/null
}

_ytmv_completion() {
    local cur prev words cword
    _init_completion -n = || return

    if [ "$cword" -eq 1 ]; then
        COMPREPLY=( $(compgen -W "get lyrics tag doctor" -- "$cur") )
        return
    fi

    local sub="${words[1]}"

    # Value slots shared by every subcommand: offer the right candidates and
    # stop, so a filename never leaks into an enum argument.
    case "$prev" in
        --profile)
            COMPREPLY=( $(compgen -W "$(_ytmv_profile_list)" -- "$cur") ); return ;;
        --id3-version)
            COMPREPLY=( $(compgen -W "3 4" -- "$cur") ); return ;;
        --id3-encoding)
            COMPREPLY=( $(compgen -W "utf16 utf8 latin1 raw-big5 raw-gbk" -- "$cur") ); return ;;
        --lrc-encoding)
            COMPREPLY=( $(compgen -W "utf-8 utf-8-sig cp950 gbk" -- "$cur") ); return ;;
        --lrc-on-unencodable)
            COMPREPLY=( $(compgen -W "strict replace" -- "$cur") ); return ;;
        --lyrics)
            COMPREPLY=( $(compgen -W "auto lrclib youtube none" -- "$cur") ); return ;;
        --out)
            _filedir -d; return ;;
        --from-file)
            _filedir; return ;;
        --artist|--track|--album|--year|--langs|--m3u|--max-height|--audio-quality|--sleep|--cover-max)
            return ;;
    esac

    local common_overrides="--id3-version --id3-encoding --lrc-encoding --lrc-on-unencodable \
--skip-lrc-sidecar --skip-embed-lyrics --embed-sylt --cover-max --skip-cover --ascii-filenames"

    case "$sub" in
        get)
            case "$cur" in
                -*) COMPREPLY=( $(compgen -W "--from-file --out --profile --audio --video \
--soft-subs --burn-subs --lyrics --langs --artist --track --album --number --m3u \
--max-height --audio-quality --cookies --force --sleep --refresh-lyrics --json \
$common_overrides" -- "$cur") ) ;;
            esac
            ;;
        lyrics)
            case "$cur" in
                -*) COMPREPLY=( $(compgen -W "--profile --artist --track --album --pick \
--force --refresh-lyrics --sleep --json $common_overrides" -- "$cur") ) ;;
                *) _filedir mp3 ;;
            esac
            ;;
        tag)
            case "$cur" in
                -*) COMPREPLY=( $(compgen -W "--profile --artist --track --album --year \
--rename --dry-run $common_overrides" -- "$cur") ) ;;
                *) _filedir ;;
            esac
            ;;
        doctor)
            case "$cur" in
                -*) COMPREPLY=( $(compgen -W "--profile --list-profiles --offline --json" \
-- "$cur") ) ;;
            esac
            ;;
    esac
}

complete -F _ytmv_completion ytmv
```
